tools.name: ads_account_get_activity_logs
tools.description:
Fetches activity log entries for an ad account, showing changes made to campaigns, ad sets, ads, and other ad objects. This mirrors the Ads Manager campaign history page, including Meta system-generated changes.

  ## When to use:
  - Call this tool when the user asks about changes, modifications, or history of their ad account or specific ad objects.
  - Call this tool when the user wants to see what happened in a time range (e.g., "what changed last week?").
  - Call this tool to find out who made specific changes to ad objects.
  - Call this tool to investigate budget, status, targeting, or creative changes.

  ## When NOT to use:
  - Do NOT use for performance metrics or delivery insights — use ads_insights tools instead.
  - Do NOT use for error diagnostics — use ads_get_errors instead.

  ## Response Guidelines:
  1. Present changes in chronological order with actor, event type, and details.
  2. Highlight the most significant changes (status changes, budget modifications).
  3. If extra_data contains old_value/new_value, show what was changed from and to.
  4. Group related changes together when presenting to the user.

  ## Event categories and their event types
  The optional `event_category` filter accepts exactly one of these categories. Each category maps to the following `event_type` values (these are the values that appear in results):
  - account: ad_review_approved, ad_review_declined, ad_account_set_business_information, ad_account_update_status, ad_account_add_user_to_role, ad_account_remove_user_from_role
  - ad: ad_review_approved, ad_review_declined, add_images, create_ad, edit_images, update_ad_creative, update_ad_friendly_name, update_ad_run_status, update_ad_run_status_to_be_set_after_review
  - ad_set: create_ad_set, update_ad_set_bidding, update_ad_set_bid_strategy, update_ad_set_bid_adjustments, update_ad_set_budget, update_ad_set_duration, update_ad_set_name, update_ad_set_run_status, update_ad_set_target_spec, update_ad_set_ad_keywords, conversion_event_updated, update_campaign_schedule, update_ad_set_learning_stage_status, update_campaign_high_demand_periods, update_campaign_budget_scheduling_state, update_campaign_conversion_goal, update_campaign_value_adjustment_rule
  - audience: create_audience, update_audience, delete_audience, share_audience, receive_audience, unshare_audience, remove_shared_audience, update_adgroup_stop_delivery, ad_account_update_audience_type_url_parameter, adaccount_update_audience_segment
  - bid: update_ad_bid_info, update_ad_bid_type, update_ad_set_bidding, update_ad_set_bid_strategy, update_ad_set_bid_adjustments
  - budget: ad_account_billing_charge, ad_account_billing_chargeback, ad_account_billing_chargeback_reversal, ad_account_billing_decline, ad_account_billing_refund, ad_account_remove_spend_limit, ad_account_reset_spend_limit, ad_account_update_spend_limit, add_funding_source, billing_event, funding_event_initiated, funding_event_successful, remove_funding_source, update_ad_set_budget, update_campaign_budget, update_campaign_group_spend_cap, update_budget_flex_toggle_status
  - campaign: create_campaign_group, update_campaign_name, update_campaign_run_status, update_campaign_group_high_demand_periods, update_campaign_group_budget_scheduling_state
  - date: update_ad_set_duration
  - status: ad_account_update_status, update_ad_run_status, update_ad_run_status_to_be_set_after_review, update_ad_set_run_status, update_campaign_run_status
  - targeting: update_ad_set_target_spec, update_ad_targets_spec
  - ad_keywords: update_ad_set_ad_keywords

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID (numeric, without "act_" prefix).

object_id.description: Optional. Filter to a specific ad object ID (campaign, ad set, ad, creative). Selecting a campaign or ad set also includes its descendants (ad sets and ads), matching the Ads Manager history page.

start_time.description: Optional. Start time in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2025-01-01T00:00:00Z"). Defaults to 3 months ago.

end_time.description: Optional. End time in ISO 8601 format. Defaults to now.

event_category.description: Optional. Filter by event category. Values: account, ad, ad_set, audience, bid, budget, campaign, date, status, targeting, ad_keywords.

user_id.description: Optional. Filter by the user who made the change.

limit.description: Optional. Maximum number of results to return (1-1000). Defaults to 100.

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

tools.name: ads_activate_entity
tools.description:
Activates a campaign, ad set, or ad by changing its status from PAUSED to ACTIVE, effectively publishing the entity.

  ## When to use:
  - Call this tool ONLY after the user has explicitly confirmed they want to publish/activate.
  - Use after the user has reviewed the entity via ads_create_campaign or ads_update_entity.
  - Supports entity_type values: "campaign", "ad_set", or "ad".

  ## When NOT to use:
  - Do NOT call without explicit user confirmation to publish.
  - Do NOT use for pausing active entities. Use ads_update_entity with fields={"status":"PAUSED"} instead. When that update returns is_draft=false, the pause was sent to the live object: do NOT call this tool to commit or verify it, even if the entity has other staged edits. This tool can undo the pause or publish unrelated changes; verify with ads_get_ad_entities instead.

  ## Status Hierarchy:
  - Activating a parent does NOT automatically activate its children. Each live entity is activated individually. Objects staged in a draft are not: read the account's draft objects to collect the campaign, ad set and ad ids, pass them together in object_ids, and the whole set publishes in one call.
  - For ads to deliver, ALL levels in the hierarchy must be ACTIVE (campaign, ad set, and ad) — including an ad published from a draft whose parents were already live.
  - Activating a child entity while its parent is paused will succeed, but the child will NOT deliver until the parent is also activated.
  - After creating a full campaign structure of live entities, activate from top to bottom: campaign first, then ad set, then ad.

  ## Response Guidelines:
  1. For live entities, when verification_hint is present, follow it to read back the configured and effective status with ads_get_ad_entities before confirming activation. Configured ACTIVE alone does not prove delivery.
  2. A PUBLISHING status means only that the objects cleared the checks this call
     runs and were handed to the publisher, which finishes afterwards. The
     publisher applies further checks of its own and can still reject an object;
     this tool is not told when that happens. Report PUBLISHING as handed off,
     never as published or live. When verification_hint is present, follow it to
     immediately poll ads_get_ad_entities for the affected draft and live objects.
     Confirm only changes observed in live read-back; disappearance
     from the draft alone is not proof. If still unverified, report pending or
     unavailable and offer Ads Manager as a fallback.
  3. If the call is rejected for validation errors, the message lists the offending
     campaign, ad set, or ad and its errors. Nothing was published. Relay the
     errors, fix them with ads_update_entity, then activate again. If the user
     would rather publish the rest now, call again with
     ignore_validation_errors=true; the broken objects stay behind in the draft.
  4. Provide the entity ID, entity type, and new status.
  5. If activating a child entity, remind the user that all parent entities must also be active for ads to deliver.

  ## CRITICAL:
  - This action makes the entity live and will start spending budget.
  - Always get explicit user confirmation before calling this tool.

  ## POTENTIAL NEXT STEP — RECOMMEND OPPORTUNITY SCORE:
  After a successful activation, suggest calling `ads_get_opportunity_score` to check
  the account's optimization status and get personalized recommendations
  from Meta to maximize ad performance while spending is active.

## Draft mode:
Draft mode is enabled for you, so the objects created via ads_create_campaign/ads_create_ad_set/ads_create_ad are staged in a draft and are NOT live yet. Publish by listing the exact objects in object_ids: everything listed is published together and nothing else is touched. Edited one ad under an already-live ad set? List that ad alone, with entity_id and entity_type naming that same ad — publishing its campaign instead would also ship every other change staged under that campaign. Built a whole campaign? List the campaign, its ad sets and its ads. List a parent only when that parent is itself still unpublished. Do not work the ids out yourself: call ads_get_ad_entities with object_state=draft, scoped by putting the object you care about in object_ids, and pass back the ad_object_id of everything it returns that you want live. The call tells you if an object has nothing staged. ONLY IF you omit object_ids: a newly-created draft child still depends on its unpublished parent, so call on the campaign (entity_type=campaign). A staged edit to an already-live campaign, ad set or ad can be published directly. Publishing applies the staged edits and nothing more, so an already-live object that is paused stays paused: set publish_as_active=true when the user asked to activate, turn on, or make the target named by entity_id live, and leave it false when they asked only to publish or apply their changes (including a staged pause). If the result carries publish_as_active_applied=false, the target was published as staged without forcing it ACTIVE: do not claim that the activation request was applied. Everything being published is validated first: if any object has a validation error the call is rejected, nothing is published, and the error names the object to fix. Relay those errors and offer to fix them; if the user instead wants the rest to go live now, call again with ignore_validation_errors=true and the broken objects are left behind. Otherwise the call returns PUBLISHING, which means the objects were handed to the publisher and it finishes afterwards. The publisher runs further checks these ones do not cover and can still reject an object; this call does not report that outcome, so do not say an object is live. When verification_hint is present, follow it to poll ads_get_ad_entities for the affected draft and live objects immediately; confirm only changes observed in live read-back. Use Ads Manager as a fallback when verification is unavailable.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID that owns the entity.

entity_id.description: The entity ID to activate (change from PAUSED to ACTIVE).

entity_type.description: The type of entity to activate. Values: campaign, ad_set, ad.

object_ids.description: Draft objects only. The exact objects to publish, listed by id. Everything you list is published together and nothing else is touched, so include every object whose staged changes you want published -- just the one ad you edited, or a campaign and its ad sets and ads. List a parent only when that parent is itself still unpublished; an object staged under an already-live parent is published on its own. To find the ids, call ads_get_ad_entities first with object_state=draft and the object you care about in object_ids: it returns every staged object under it, and their ad_object_id values are what you pass here.

items.description: Campaign, ad set or ad id.

ignore_validation_errors.description: Draft publishes only. Defaults to false, which rejects the publish when any object being published has a validation error. Set to true only when the user has seen those errors and asked to publish anyway: the rest is published with the broken objects skipped, and they stay in the draft.

publish_as_active.description: Draft publishes only. Defaults to false, which publishes the staged edits exactly as staged: an already-live object keeps its current run status, so a paused campaign stays paused. Set to true when the user asked to activate, turn on, or make the target named by entity_id live. Only that target is set ACTIVE; other objects published in the same call keep their staged status. When object_ids is present, it must include entity_id. Leave this false when the user asked only to publish or apply their changes, including a staged pause. The result reports publish_as_active_applied; when it is false the target was published as staged and keeps its current status. Ignored for entities with nothing staged, which are activated either way.

tools.name: ads_boost_ig_post
tools.description:
Creates an Instagram ad from an existing IG post. Supports a plan/confirm two-step flow.

  Required: ad_account_id, ig_account_id, and ig_media_id unless another field already identifies the post. That is enough for a simple profile boost; other goals can require a promoted_object naming a page, pixel, conversion, or application. For full control, override campaign (L3), ad set (L2), or ad (L1) fields using compatible combinations.

  ## When to use:
  - Call with confirmed=false FIRST to get a plan showing all resolved settings.
  - Call with confirmed=true ONLY after the user has reviewed and approved the plan.
  - For an ordinary boost, use after ads_get_ig_accounts and ads_get_ig_media to get the required IDs.

  ## When NOT to use:
  - Do NOT call with confirmed=true without first showing the user the plan.
  - Do NOT use for creating regular (non-IG-boost) ad campaigns — use ads_create_campaign instead.

  ## Response Guidelines:
  1. In plan mode: Show all resolved settings across L3/L2/L1, including defaults.
  2. In creation mode: Return all created entity IDs and confirm PAUSED state.
  3. Remind user they can activate with ads_activate_entity when ready.

  ## Call to action:
  - Use call_to_action_type plus the optional call_to_action_value object. Don't use call_to_action field; it's deprecated.
  - Website CTAs (LEARN_MORE, SHOP_NOW, WATCH_MORE, CONTACT_US, BOOK_NOW, SIGN_UP, SEE_DETAILS) need call_to_action_value.link.
  - VIEW_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE links to the boosting account's profile automatically.
  - Messaging CTAs build their destination automatically and need the matching destination_type: INSTAGRAM_MESSAGE with INSTAGRAM_DIRECT, WHATSAPP_MESSAGE with WHATSAPP (the account must have a linked WhatsApp Business number), MESSAGE_PAGE with MESSENGER.
  - Without call_to_action_type the ad uses VIEW_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, even when destination_type is a messaging destination. Pass the matching messaging CTA to get a message button.
  - To learn more about Instagram ad goals and their CTAs, see https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1058474831011088.
  - For every call to action type Meta supports, see https://www.facebook.com/business/help/410873986524407. This tool accepts only the call_to_action_type enum values.

  ## CRITICAL:
  - All entities are created in PAUSED state. Budget is NOT spent until activated.
  - Always show the plan first and get explicit user confirmation before creating.
  - The ig_account_id must be linked to the ad_account_id and the app must have `instagram_basic` permission for it. Use ads_get_ig_accounts to find eligible accounts.
  - Defaults: roughly the $5 USD/day-equivalent in the ad account's local currency for 6 days, OUTCOME_TRAFFIC objective, INSTAGRAM_PROFILE destination, US targeting, IMPRESSIONS billing, LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP bidding.
  - All budget amounts are in the smallest unit of the ad account's currency (e.g. cents for USD, whole yen for JPY). The plan output includes a `currency` field — present budgets in that currency, never assume USD.
  - A campaign budget (campaign_daily_budget or campaign_lifetime_budget) moves budget and bidding to the campaign: do not also send daily_budget, lifetime_budget, bid_strategy, or bid_amount, and use campaign_bid_strategy for bidding.
  - The ad must run for at least 24 hours and at most 365 days.

  ## Objective, destination, and performance goal:
  - Profile visits: OUTCOME_TRAFFIC + INSTAGRAM_PROFILE + VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE.
  - Reach: OUTCOME_AWARENESS + UNDEFINED + REACH (or IMPRESSIONS).
  - Post engagement: OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT + ON_POST + POST_ENGAGEMENT.
  - Video views: OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT + ON_VIDEO + THRUPLAY.
  - An omitted destination_type or optimization_goal defaults from the objective: OUTCOME_TRAFFIC uses INSTAGRAM_PROFILE + VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE (WEBSITE + LINK_CLICKS for a website destination or goal); OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT uses ON_POST + POST_ENGAGEMENT (ON_VIDEO for video-view goals); OUTCOME_AWARENESS uses UNDEFINED + REACH; OUTCOME_LEADS and OUTCOME_SALES use WEBSITE + OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS; OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION uses APP + APP_INSTALLS. A destination_type given without a goal gets that destination's usual goal, else the objective's default when the destination allows it, else the one goal the destination allows for the account, for example PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT (or LINK_CLICKS) for engagement on INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, LEAD_GENERATION for leads on MESSENGER, and QUALITY_CALL on PHONE_CALL; only when none of these applies does the error list the valid goals. A goal the default destination cannot take, such as a messaging or profile goal, needs an explicit destination_type. Values you provide must be compatible with each other. Account and media eligibility also apply.
  - ON_AD is a lead-form destination, not a destination for post engagement or video views. FACEBOOK is not a supported destination for this tool.
  - Promoted-object prerequisites are checked during planning. When a page is required and can be resolved from the linked Instagram account, the plan includes it. Otherwise supply the required promoted_object fields before confirming.

## Partnership Ads (branded content):
- A Partnership Ad promotes a post authored by a *creator* on behalf of a brand. ig_account_id remains the advertiser's linked brand IG account used for ad creation and the brand-side permission check, while ig_media_id identifies the creator-owned post. Creator media may not appear in ads_get_ig_media for the advertiser's account.
- When verification succeeds, the Partnership Ad displays the creator as its primary identity and credits the advertiser's brand as sponsor.
- Pass the creator-owned post as ig_media_id, or pass ad_code when the creator issued a per-post code. An ad_code identifies the post by itself, so ig_media_id is not needed with it.
- Do NOT pass sponsor_id or ad_code to boost a post the advertiser authored themselves — that is an ordinary boost.
- After creation, inspect partnership_ad_verification_status. A value of verified means the server derived an existing-post Partnership Ad. For not_partnership_ad, unexpected_partnership_ad_type, or unverifiable, relay the returned message and do not retry creation or activate the ad automatically. is_partnership_ad is null when verification could not complete.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID to create the boost under. Format: numeric ID.

ig_account_id.description: The advertiser's linked IG account used for ad creation.

ig_media_id.description: The numeric ID of the post to boost. For an ordinary boost, use the `id` field from `ads_get_ig_media` exactly as returned; do NOT decode or transform the permalink URL shortcode. Required for an ordinary boost.

daily_budget.description: Daily budget in the smallest unit of the ad account currency (e.g. cents for USD, whole yen for JPY). Defaults to roughly the $5 USD/day-equivalent in the account currency, clamped to the per-currency minimum. Mutually exclusive with lifetime_budget. Omit when using a campaign budget.

duration_days.description: Number of days to run the ad, from start_time or from creation. Default: 6. Minimum 1, maximum 365.

call_to_action_type.description: CTA button type. VIEW_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE and the messaging CTAs (INSTAGRAM_MESSAGE, WHATSAPP_MESSAGE, MESSAGE_PAGE) derive their value; the others are website CTAs that need call_to_action_value.link.

call_to_action_value.description: Optional value object for call_to_action_type. Website CTAs need link; VIEW_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE and messaging CTAs take no value fields.

url_tags.description: Tracking parameters appended to the ad's destination link, e.g. "utm_source=ig&utm_campaign=spring". Pass the query string only, without a leading "?".

objective.description: Campaign objective. Default: OUTCOME_TRAFFIC. Only Outcome-Driven objectives are accepted: OUTCOME_AWARENESS, OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT, OUTCOME_LEADS, OUTCOME_SALES, OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION. Pair it with a compatible destination_type and optimization_goal; see the tool description.

campaign_name.description: Name for the campaign. Default: "Instagram post: {caption}" derived from the IG post.

buying_type.description: Campaign buying type. Default: AUCTION. Values: AUCTION, RESERVED.

special_ad_categories.description: JSON array of special ad categories. Default: []. Values: NONE, EMPLOYMENT, HOUSING, FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES, ISSUES_ELECTIONS_POLITICS, ONLINE_GAMBLING_AND_GAMING. HOUSING also covers mortgages and other home loans. CREDIT is retired: use FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES for other credit, loans, insurance and financial products. Use these exact values, not display names.

campaign_bid_strategy.description: Campaign-level bid strategy. Values: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP, LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, COST_CAP.

campaign_daily_budget.description: Campaign-level daily budget in the smallest unit of the ad account currency (e.g. cents for USD, whole yen for JPY). Mutually exclusive with campaign_lifetime_budget.

campaign_lifetime_budget.description: Campaign-level lifetime budget in the smallest unit of the ad account currency (e.g. cents for USD, whole yen for JPY). Mutually exclusive with campaign_daily_budget.

ad_set_name.description: Name for the ad set. Default: "Instagram post: {caption}" derived from the IG post.

destination_type.description: Ad set destination type. Default depends on objective: INSTAGRAM_PROFILE for OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, ON_POST for OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT, UNDEFINED for OUTCOME_AWARENESS, WEBSITE for OUTCOME_LEADS and OUTCOME_SALES, APP for OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION. Use UNDEFINED for awareness/reach, ON_POST for engagement/POST_ENGAGEMENT, and ON_VIDEO for engagement/THRUPLAY. Other destinations require compatible goals: WEBSITE, ON_AD (lead forms), INSTAGRAM_DIRECT, MESSENGER, WHATSAPP. ON_AD is not a destination for post engagement, and FACEBOOK is not supported.

optimization_goal.description: Ad set optimization goal. Default depends on objective and destination_type: VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE for OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, POST_ENGAGEMENT for OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT, REACH for OUTCOME_AWARENESS, OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS for OUTCOME_LEADS and OUTCOME_SALES, APP_INSTALLS for OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION; a destination_type with one valid goal for the account gets that goal. Values: VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, LINK_CLICKS, POST_ENGAGEMENT, THRUPLAY, CONVERSATIONS, LEAD_GENERATION, OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, REACH, IMPRESSIONS, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, APP_INSTALLS, QUALITY_CALL, PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT. For post engagement use OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT + ON_POST + POST_ENGAGEMENT; for engagement video views use ON_VIDEO + THRUPLAY; for awareness REACH or IMPRESSIONS use UNDEFINED, WEBSITE, or a messaging destination (INSTAGRAM_DIRECT, MESSENGER, WHATSAPP).

billing_event.description: Ad set billing event. Default: IMPRESSIONS. Values: IMPRESSIONS, LINK_CLICKS, POST_ENGAGEMENT, VIDEO_VIEWS.

bid_strategy.description: Ad set bid strategy. Default: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP. Values: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP, LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, COST_CAP. Omit when using a campaign budget; use campaign_bid_strategy instead.

bid_amount.description: Bid cap in the smallest unit of the ad account currency (e.g. cents for USD, whole yen for JPY). Used with LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP bid strategy. Omit when using a campaign budget.

lifetime_budget.description: Ad set lifetime budget in the smallest unit of the ad account currency (e.g. cents for USD, whole yen for JPY). Mutually exclusive with daily_budget. Requires end_time. Omit when using a campaign budget.

start_time.description: Ad set start time in ISO 8601 format or Unix seconds. Default: when the ad is created.

end_time.description: Ad set end time in ISO 8601 format or Unix seconds. Default: start plus duration_days. Must be at least 24 hours after the start (or after creation when start_time is omitted or past) and within 365 days.

promoted_object.description: JSON promoted object spec. Required fields depend on objective, destination_type, and optimization_goal: page_id for page-based goals, pixel_id/custom_event_type or custom_conversion_id for website conversions, application_id/object_store_url for app goals. Planning validates these prerequisites and includes an inferred linked page when supported. Example: {"pixel_id":"123456","custom_event_type":"PURCHASE"}.

ad_name.description: Name for the ad. Default: "Instagram post: {caption}" derived from the IG post.

sponsor_id.description: Partnership Ads only. The brand's IG account ID, when the brand holds ongoing permission from the post's creator.

ad_code.description: Partnership Ads only. The per-post code the creator issued to this brand. Names the post, so ig_media_id is not needed.

confirmed.description: Set to true to create the ad. Set to false (default) to get a plan showing resolved settings without creating anything.

tools.name: ads_catalog_create
tools.description: Creates a catalog: a structured inventory of products or other items and their details that Meta can rank and show in ads. It is best for advertisers with multiple or frequently changing items who want personalized promotion at scale: Advantage+ catalog ads dynamically select products for prospecting or retargeting, while Product Extensions keep an image or video ad and add relevant catalog products below it. Check `ads_catalog_list_catalogs` first and reuse a suitable catalog when possible. Optionally upload one feed URL, inline item batch, or file; omit product data to create an empty catalog.

business_id.description: Always required. The Meta Business Manager ID to create the catalog under. This must be a Business Manager ID, NOT an ad account ID and NOT a Page ID. Look it up with ads_catalog_list_catalogs or in Meta Business Settings if unknown.

catalog_name.description: Always required. Name for the new catalog. If the user did not specify one, ask them for it instead of calling this tool without it.

vertical.description: Catalog vertical (e.g., commerce, vehicles, hotels). Defaults to commerce.

feed_name.description: Name for the product feed. Required when using feed_url.

feed_password.description: Password for authenticated feed URL access (HTTP basic auth or SFTP). Only used with feed_url.

schedule.description: Feed schedule configuration. Only used with feed_url.

interval.description: Upload frequency: hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly.

timezone.description: Timezone for the schedule. Defaults to America/Los_Angeles.

day_of_week.description: Day of week for weekly schedules (e.g., monday).

data.description: Product fields as string-to-string entries (id, title, description, price, availability, image_link, link, brand, condition, etc.).

update_only.description: If true, the upload only updates existing items instead of creating new ones. Defaults to false.

tools.name: ads_catalog_create_feed_rule
tools.description:
Create a new transformation rule on a product feed. Feed rules map or transform attributes during ingestion to fix common feed schema mismatches without the advertiser editing their source file.

When to use:
- The advertiser's feed column name does not match a Meta product attribute (use mapping_rule, e.g. params={"map_from": "desc"} on attribute="description").
- A specific value needs translation (use value_mapping_rule, e.g. map "yes"/"no" availability values to "in stock"/"out of stock").
- Letter case needs normalization (use letter_case_rule with type=to_upper|to_lower|capitalize_all|capitalize_first).
- A default value should be filled in when the feed leaves a column empty (use fallback_rule with user_default_value).
- A regex find/replace is needed on values (use regex_replace_rule).

When NOT to use:
- To inspect existing rules on a feed (use ads_catalog_get_feed_rules).
- To upload or modify feed data itself (use the catalog ingestion endpoints).
- To create a catalog, feed, or product set (use ads_catalog_create for a catalog, ads_catalog_create_product_feed for a feed, ads_catalog_create_product_set for a product set).

Notes:
- params is a JSON-encoded object of string-to-string key-value pairs, e.g. {"map_from": "desc"}.
- Both attribute and rule_type are immutable after creation; only params can be updated later via a separate endpoint.
- The combination (product_feed_id, rule_type, attribute) must be unique. Re-creating the same combination returns a duplicate error.

product_feed_id.description: The ID of the product feed to attach this rule to (numeric string).

attribute.description: The catalog attribute the rule transforms (e.g., "description", "availability", "title", "price"). A feed cannot have more than one rule with the same rule_type and attribute. Immutable once created.

rule_type.description: The type of rule. One of: "mapping_rule" (map a source column to a catalog attribute, e.g. params={"map_from": "desc"}); "value_mapping_rule" (map raw input values to catalog values for a specific attribute); "letter_case_rule" (transform letter case; params={"type": "to_upper|to_lower|capitalize_all|capitalize_first"}); "fallback_rule" (use params={"user_default_value": "..."} when the input value is empty); "regex_replace_rule" (regex-based find/replace on values). Immutable once created.

params.description: Optional JSON-encoded object of string-to-string key-value parameters for the rule, e.g. {"map_from": "desc"} for a mapping_rule or {"type": "to_lower"} for a letter_case_rule. Common keys: "map_from" (mapping_rule source column), "type" (letter_case_rule mode), "user_default_value" (fallback_rule default), "dependent_field_name", "dependent_field_value", "map_mode" (COPY|MOVE). String values are stored verbatim (whitespace preserved). If omitted, defaults to an empty object.

tools.name: ads_catalog_create_product_feed
tools.description:
Create a new product feed (a "data source") under a catalog. A product feed is the entry point for ingesting product data into a catalog, either by uploading a file or by pointing Meta at a URL to fetch on a recurring schedule. This complements ads_catalog_create, which creates the catalog itself.

When to use:
- The advertiser wants to add a new source of products to an existing catalog.
- The advertiser wants Meta to fetch a feed file (CSV/TSV/XML) from a URL on a recurring schedule (pass the schedule object).
- Setting up a feed before uploading items or attaching feed rules.

When NOT to use:
- To create the catalog itself (use ads_catalog_create).
- To upload items into an existing feed right now (use the catalog ingestion / upload-session endpoints).
- To add transformation rules to an existing feed (use ads_catalog_create_feed_rule).
- To inspect existing feeds (use ads_catalog_list_product_feeds).

Notes:
- schedule is optional. When omitted, the feed is created with no automatic fetch schedule. When provided, it is a structured object; "interval" and "url" are always required and (S)FTP URLs additionally require "username"/"password". "DAILY" requires "hour"; "WEEKLY" requires "hour" and "day_of_week"; "MONTHLY" requires "hour" and "day_of_month"; "HOURLY" requires none of these timing fields. Example: {"interval":"DAILY","hour":6,"url":"https://example.com/feed.csv"}.
- If the feed is created successfully but the schedule fails to attach, use ads_catalog_update_product_feed with replace_schedule to add the schedule to the existing feed. Do not create a duplicate feed.
- The feed is created under the catalog identified by catalog_id; the output id is the new feed's Meta-assigned ID.
- Requires EDIT_PRODUCT_CATALOG permission on the catalog.

catalog_id.description: The ID of the catalog to create the product feed under (numeric string).

name.description: A human-readable name for the product feed (e.g. "Summer 2026 Catalog Feed").

feed_type.description: Optional feed type. Most commerce/product catalogs can omit this to use the catalog's default item type. Use lowercase feed type values such as "products" (the default), "hotel", "flight", "destination", "home_listing", "vehicles", or "media_title". Uppercase aliases are accepted and normalized. Must be valid for the catalog's vertical.

country.description: Optional ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the feed (e.g. "US", "GB"). Defaults to "US" when omitted.

default_currency.description: Optional ISO 4217 currency code used for items in the feed that do not specify their own currency (e.g. "USD", "GBP"). Defaults to "USD" when omitted.

schedule.description: Optional recurring schedule for fetching the feed from a URL. Omit it to create a feed with no automatic fetch schedule (items can still be uploaded manually). When provided, "interval" and "url" are always required, and (S)FTP URLs additionally require "username"/"password". "DAILY" requires "hour"; "WEEKLY" requires "hour" and "day_of_week"; "MONTHLY" requires "hour" and "day_of_month"; "HOURLY" requires none of these timing fields. Example: {"interval":"DAILY","hour":6,"url":"https://example.com/feed.csv"}.

url.description: Required. The HTTP(S)/(S)FTP location to fetch the feed file from.

interval_count.description: Optional multiplier for interval (1-255, default 1; e.g. every N days).

hour.description: Hour of day (0-23) to fetch. Required for "DAILY", "WEEKLY", and "MONTHLY". Optional for "HOURLY", where it defaults to the current hour in "timezone".

minute.description: Optional minute of the hour (0-59) to fetch. Defaults to 0 for "DAILY", "WEEKLY", and "MONTHLY", and to the current minute for "HOURLY".

day_of_week.description: Day of week to fetch (e.g. "MONDAY"). Required for "WEEKLY" and not used by other intervals.

day_of_month.description: Day of month to fetch (1-31). Required for "MONTHLY" and not used by other intervals.

timezone.description: Timezone for the schedule (e.g. "America/Los_Angeles"; defaults to America/Los_Angeles).

tools.name: ads_catalog_create_product_feed_upload_session
tools.description:
Triggers a new upload session on an existing product feed, forcing an immediate refresh from the configured remote source URL. Returns the new upload session ID for polling via `ads_catalog_get_product_feed_upload_sessions`.

Only works for feeds with a remote fetch URL configured — check with `ads_catalog_list_product_feeds` first; a feed with no source URL cannot start a session.

## When to use:
- Refresh / re-pull / re-ingest products from an existing remote feed without waiting for the scheduled run (e.g. after fixing the source file or updating the hosted feed).

## When NOT to use:
- Feed has no source URL (manual/batch-only catalog) → `ads_catalog_update_product_feed` with `replace_schedule` first.
- Creating a new feed → `ads_catalog_create_product_feed`; inspecting past runs → `ads_catalog_get_product_feed_upload_sessions`; changing schedule/URL/credentials → `ads_catalog_update_product_feed`.

## Errors:
- No source URL → fails, nothing to fetch. Concurrent upload running → fails "upload already in progress": do NOT retry immediately; wait or poll `ads_catalog_get_product_feed_upload_sessions`.

## Shared resources:
Fetch via resources/read: `catalog://id-conventions`, `catalog://errors`.

tools.name: ads_catalog_create_product_set
tools.description:
Creates a dynamic product set from a structured filter and returns the set ID + matched count. Always preview the filter with `ads_catalog_list_products` first — set creation mutates the catalog with no undo via this tool.

## When to use:
- User explicitly confirmed they want to create a product set from a filter already previewed via `ads_catalog_list_products`.
- User wants to materialize a catalog segment defined by product attributes.

## When NOT to use:
- Filter not yet confirmed → call `ads_catalog_list_products` first and surface sample + total_count.
- Static set of explicit product IDs → not supported yet.
- Update existing set → `ads_catalog_update_product_set`.

## Identifier types
See `catalog://id-conventions` via resources/read.

## Input
- `catalog_id` required (call `ads_catalog_list_catalogs` first if you don't have it), `name` required non-empty, `filter` required.

See `catalog://filter-spec` via resources/read.

- `retailer_id` is optional and should be set only if the user explicitly provides it.
- See `catalog://errors` via resources/read for duplicate/rejection handling.

## Returns
- `product_set_id`, `catalog_id`, `name`, `product_count`, `filter_rule`, etc.

- `catalog://id-conventions` via resources/read
- `catalog://errors` via resources/read

tools.name: ads_catalog_delete_product
tools.description:
Delete existing catalog items from one catalog through a batch-shaped request. Supply `catalog_id` once and identify each item by its merchant-defined `retailer_id` in `items`.

When to use:
- A merchant wants to permanently remove catalog items that should no longer appear in ads or on Meta surfaces.
- You know the catalog ID and each retailer ID, usually from `ads_catalog_list_products`.

When NOT to use:
- To hide an item reversibly, use `ads_catalog_update_product` with `visibility="hidden"`.
- To mark an item unavailable, use `ads_catalog_update_product` with `availability="out of stock"`.
- To delete a product set, use `ads_catalog_product_set_delete`.
- To delete an entire catalog, use Commerce Manager because MCP does not support that operation.

Inputs and results:
- `catalog_id` identifies the catalog that owns every submitted item.
- `items` contains objects with a required `retailer_id`. Empty and oversized batches fail before execution.
- Results include submitted, accepted, and rejected counts, ordered validation details, and ordered successful deletion results.
- Unknown retailer IDs are rejected individually while accepted items continue. Every occurrence of a duplicated retailer ID is rejected.
- `SOURCE_MAY_OVERWRITE`: the listed feed, partner platform or website still supplies the item and can add it back. Warn the user to remove it there to ensure it is deleted.

Timeouts:
- If a call times out or fails with a server error and returns no result, some items may already have been applied. Retry the same items in smaller calls of about half the previous batch size. Retrying is safe: already-deleted items return `UNKNOWN_RETAILER_ID` rejections, creates upsert, and updates reapply the same values.

Deletion is permanent and cannot be undone through the API. Recreating an item requires supplying its details again.

The current synchronous per-call cap is 25.

catalog_id.description: The catalog that owns every submitted item.

items.description: Existing retailer IDs to delete permanently.

tools.name: ads_catalog_event_source_connect
tools.description:
Connect an event source to a product catalog so its signals can be matched against the catalog's products (for dynamic ads and Advantage+ catalog ads). Event sources are also commonly called "pixels" or "datasets"; the source can be a PIXEL (data from the seller's website), an APP (data from the seller's app), or an OFFLINE_CONVERSION_DATA_SET (data from in-store transactions). The Conversions API (CAPI) is an enhancement that augments PIXEL or APP data — it is not a standalone event source type.
To pick which source to connect, use ads_catalog_event_source_get_recommendations.

Matching only happens for connected sources: a dataset's event content IDs are matched against the catalog's product retailer IDs only when that pixel/dataset is connected to the catalog.
If the dataset tools (e.g. ads_get_dataset_details, ads_get_dataset_quality) show content IDs are being sent, check ads_catalog_event_source_get_health to verify that they are matching products in the catalog (`match_rate`).

- The advertiser wants to connect a pixel / event source to a catalog (e.g. after ads_catalog_event_source_get shows an expected source is missing).

When NOT to use:
- To list the event sources already connected to a catalog (use ads_catalog_event_source_get).

- To find which catalogs an event source is connected to (use ads_catalog_event_source_get_catalogs).

- The operation is idempotent: connecting an already-connected source succeeds and returns already_connected=true without making a change.

tools.name: ads_catalog_event_source_get_health
tools.description:
Report the match rate and setup issues for the event sources connected to a product catalog. "Match rate" is the percentage of conversion events (e.g. Purchase, AddToCart) whose content IDs matched a product in the catalog — higher match rates mean better ad targeting and measurement.

Each event source has a source_type: PIXEL (data from the seller's website), APP (data from the seller's app), or OFFLINE_CONVERSION_DATA_SET (data from in-store transactions); the Conversions API (CAPI) is an enhancement that augments PIXEL or APP data, not a standalone source type.

This tool returns the latest overall match rate (match_rate) AND the historical per-date, per-event-type match rate stats over the past 28 days (match_rate_stats). The historical data is useful to detect trends, regressions, or sudden changes in match quality over time. It also returns a list of setup issues (each with a type, description, and severity). This is the same measurement-layer data Commerce Manager surfaces in its "Events" tab.

When to use:
- To diagnose why catalog products are not matching signals / events ("low match rate", "events not matching products")
- To detect match rate trends or regressions over the past month
- To list the setup issues for a pixel / event source connected to a catalog
- To report match quality for one event source (pass event_source_id) or all connected sources (omit it)

When NOT to use:
- To just list which event sources are connected, without health data (use ads_catalog_event_source_get)
- To check feed-level catalog diagnostics like broken images or missing fields (use ads_catalog_get_diagnostics)
- To run Dynamic Ads integration health checks (use ads_catalog_get_dynamic_ads_health)

tools.name: ads_catalog_get_diagnostics
tools.description:
Fetches diagnostic issues for a product catalog, including errors and warnings that may affect ad delivery.

## When to use:
- User reports catalog issues or products not showing in ads; asks about catalog errors, warnings, or quality issues (broken images, missing fields, policy violations).
- Diagnosing why products may not be eligible for certain ad surfaces.
- Catalog-level broken/failed product images (for per-product image status, also check `image_fetch_status` from `ads_catalog_list_products`).

## When NOT to use:
- Individual product details → `ads_catalog_list_products`.
- Feed rules / why catalog data differs from the feed file → `ads_catalog_get_feed_rules`.
- Stale/failing store sync (Shopify/WooCommerce/Magento) → `ads_catalog_list_partner_integrations` (connection failure, not item quality).
- Why a SPECIFIC product is not_eligible for Dynamic Ads → `ads_catalog_list_products` with that product's ID as `entity_id`; the per-item `issues`. This tool only reports catalog-level aggregates, not the per-item blocking reasons.

## Response Guidelines:
Prioritize MUST_FIX over OPPORTUNITY; explain each diagnostic with corrective actions; group related ones. `number_of_affected_items` counts VARIANTS/SKUs, never "products" — do not compare or sum across issues. When `affected_channels` is non-empty the issue affects only those channels ("mini_shops" = FB/IG Shops, "da" = Dynamic Ads, "marketplace" = FB Marketplace, "ig_shopping" = IG Shopping, "whatsapp" = WhatsApp catalog); empty means broad. Do not overstate severity. To find affected products, try `ads_catalog_list_products` with `error_type` (best-effort).

tools.name: ads_catalog_get_dynamic_ads_health
tools.description:
Run Dynamic Ads (DA) integration health checks for either a product catalog OR a single product set. Each check returns pass/fail.

## Scope (catalog vs product set):
- `catalog_id` → catalog-level checks: pixel/event source setup, match rate, eligible product count, DA configuration issues.
- `product_set_id` → creative-quality checks for the set (e.g. slideshow/video quality), NOT catalog-wide DA setup. Owning catalog resolves automatically. At least one of the two is required; if both are given, `product_set_id` wins. Response echoes `scope` so you can confirm which ran.
- Different from `ads_catalog_get_diagnostics`: that reports item-level data quality (missing images, feed errors, policy violations); this checks DA / creative-quality health.

## When to use:
- DA setup health/readiness for a catalog; "why are my Dynamic Ads not working?", "is my catalog set up for DA?"; DA not delivering or poor performance; pixel setup / event source / match rate issues; creative quality of a product set.

## When NOT to use:
- Item-level diagnostics → `ads_catalog_get_diagnostics`; individual products → `ads_catalog_list_products`; feed rules → `ads_catalog_get_feed_rules`; set membership → `ads_catalog_list_products` with the set ID.

## Response Guidelines:
Prioritize failed checks; explain each with corrective actions; group related ones. MUST_FIX first. All pass → confirm healthy. Use `action_uri` for the Commerce Manager link. Item-level issues → suggest `ads_catalog_get_diagnostics` separately.

tools.description:

tools.name: ads_catalog_list_products
tools.description:
Preferred Ads catalog reader for browsing, attribute search, and affected-item search. Reads a catalog, set, or item via `entity_id`; a single-item read returns a one-row page. Use before set creation to preview matching items.

## What `entity_id` can be:
- catalog ID → products matching filter, paginated.
- set ID → products in set, filter AND'd onto set rule.
- item ID → that one product, filter/limit/cursor ignored.

## Identifier types
See `catalog://id-conventions` via resources/read.

## When to use:
- List/browse/search products in catalog → pass `entity_id=<catalog_id>` (e.g. "what's in my catalog?", "show out-of-stock").
- Find affected items → get a diagnostic type from `ads_catalog_get_diagnostics`, then pass it separately as `error_type`; add `filter` to narrow the affected items. For lightweight discovery, request `fields=["retailer_id","name"]`; product_id is always included.
- List each Shopify product once → pass `view=product_groups`. Each row is the
  best matching item variant for its group, not a canonical representative.
- Count matches before set creation via `page_info.total_count`.
- List products ingested by a specific feed → use a product-feed filter.
- List products ranked by Product Views → use `top_products=all`; use
  `top_products=missing_video` to prioritize video coverage work.
- See inside existing product set → pass `entity_id=<product_set_id>`.
- Fetch full details of one known product → pass `entity_id=<product_id>`.
- Debug per-product issues (missing fields, prices, availability, image_fetch_status).
- Inspect a product's Dynamic Ads issues: `dynamic_ads_eligibility` and per-item `issues[]` reason codes are returned by default; when `not_eligible`, `issues[]` lists the must-fix blocking reasons.

## When NOT to use:
- Which sets contain a product → `ads_catalog_list_product_sets` with `entity_id=<product_id>`.
- List/inspect sets themselves → `ads_catalog_list_product_sets`.
- Catalog-level diagnostic summaries/counts → `ads_catalog_get_diagnostics`, overview → `ads_catalog_list_catalogs`. If an error_type cannot be filtered, report the limitation and diagnostic count; do not present an unfiltered page as affected items.
- No text-search parameter — build a product filter from the requested attributes.
- Performance analysis beyond the returned ranking evidence → use Product Insights.


See `catalog://filter-spec` via resources/read.

- `limit` default 20 max 100, `cursor`, `fields`, `error_type`, `top_products` separate AND — see `catalog://errors` via resources/read and `catalog://pagination` via resources/read.

## Examples
- Catalog all: `entity_id=<catalog_id>`, omit `filter`.
- Catalog SKU lookup: `entity_id=<catalog_id>`, `filter={"retailer_id":{"eq":"ABC-001"}}`.
- Top products without video: `entity_id=<catalog_id>`, `top_products=missing_video`.
- Shopify products once each: `entity_id=<catalog_id>`, `view=product_groups`.
- Single item: `entity_id=<product_id>`.
- What's in set: `entity_id=<product_set_id>`.

- `catalog://id-conventions` via resources/read
- `catalog://pagination` via resources/read
- `catalog://errors` via resources/read

tools.name: ads_catalog_product_create
tools.description:
Create or upsert catalog items through a batch-shaped request with one `catalog_id` and nested `items[]`. The catalog vertical determines each item type.

## When to use:
- Add one or more items to an existing catalog with a known catalog ID.

## When NOT to use:
- Create a catalog and initial items → `ads_catalog_create`; update only existing items → `ads_catalog_update_product`; saved filter → `ads_catalog_create_product_set`.

## Inputs:
- `catalog_id` is required. `items[]` contains nested objects; each object requires `retailer_id` and `name`.
- Optional nested fields include description, URLs, prices, currency, availability, condition, brand, visibility, and `properties`.
- Existing retailer IDs are updated. Invalid items are rejected individually, and results preserve submission order.
- Successful results include `product_id` when immediately resolved. Otherwise, find it with `ads_catalog_list_products`.
- Empty and oversized batches fail before execution.

## Timeouts:
- If a call times out or fails with a server error and returns no result, some items may already have been applied. Retry the same items in smaller calls of about half the previous batch size. Retrying is safe: already-deleted items return `UNKNOWN_RETAILER_ID` rejections, creates upsert, and updates reapply the same values.

Fetch via resources/read: `catalog://product-write-fields`, `catalog://id-conventions`, `catalog://errors`.

tools.name: ads_catalog_update_catalog
tools.description:
Update an existing catalog's settings, and set up, change or TEST the checkout URL that hands buyers off to the seller's own website to pay. This is the only tool that can test a catalog's checkout URL: it reads the URL already saved on the catalog and runs a real cart through it. At least one field besides catalog_id must be provided.

When to use:
- To rename a catalog
- To set up or change a checkout URL. Removing one is not supported here. Pass setup_checkout_url=true as soon as you know that is what the seller wants — it returns the setup card, which collects the URL, runs a real test cart and saves. Do NOT ask them to paste the URL in chat. If your client cannot render cards the call fails with an error saying so, and you then collect the URL in chat and drive the steps below yourself.
- To test a checkout URL the catalog already has saved. Pass checkout_url_test_only alone. You do not need the seller to paste the URL and you must not hand-build example links instead — this tool reads the saved URL and runs a real cart through it.

A seller who names a catalog or gives its id has told you everything this tool needs: call it directly. Do not read the catalog with ads_catalog_list_catalogs first, and do not ask the seller any checkout URL question yourself — the card asks only the questions still open for that catalog.

Checkout URL setup is still rolling out and is not available to every account yet. A checkout URL call on an account that is not in the rollout comes back unauthorized. Tell the seller it is not available for their account yet; there is no way to turn it on for them, including through their Meta contact. Renaming is unaffected and always works.

Checkout URL steps, by what you pass alongside catalog_id:
- setup_checkout_url=true: returns the setup card. Saves nothing, always safe. Pass it on its own — adding checkout_url_test_only suppresses the card and starts a real crawl instead.
- checkout_url_test_only alone: runs a test cart through the saved URL without saving. Returns a checkout_validation_result_id.
- checkout_base_url + checkout_url_test_only: runs a test cart without saving. Returns a checkout_validation_result_id.
- checkout_validation_result_id: reads back the outcome of a test already running.
- checkout_base_url alone: saves the URL and starts the crawl that monitors it from then on.

Testing is asynchronous: a test returns progress=IN_PROGRESS and the outcome lands within a few minutes. Poll it yourself in this same conversation — call again with checkout_validation_result_id about every 15 seconds until it resolves, for up to about 4 minutes, which is the cadence and ceiling the setup card uses. - To view catalog details without changing anything (use ads_catalog_list_catalogs)
- To delete a catalog — not supported via MCP
- To remove a checkout URL — not supported via MCP. Saving a different URL replaces it, but there is no way to clear one from here

tools.name: ads_catalog_update_product
tools.description:
Update existing catalog items through a batch-shaped request with one `catalog_id` and nested `items[]`. Only supplied fields are changed.

Accepted request example: `{"catalog_id":"1234567890","items":[{"retailer_id":"SKU-123","name":"Wool coat","description":"Warm wool coat","url":"https://example.com/products/SKU-123","image_url":"https://example.com/images/SKU-123.jpg","price":"129.99","sale_price":"99.99","currency":"USD","availability":"in stock","condition":"new","brand":"Northstar","visibility":"published","properties":{"custom_label_0":"winter"}}]}`

## Identifying items:
Each nested item requires `retailer_id`, the merchant's SKU or content ID. The Meta-assigned product item ID is not accepted. Unknown retailer IDs are rejected, never created.

## When to use:
- Change item fields or hide items reversibly with `visibility="hidden"`; `visibility="published"` restores them.

## When NOT to use:
- Create items → `ads_catalog_product_create`; inspect values → `ads_catalog_list_products`; edit sets, feeds, or catalogs → dedicated tools.

## Batch and field rules:
- Each item needs one effective update. Price fields require `currency` in the same nested item.
- Public availability values: `in stock`, `out of stock`, `preorder`, `available for order`, `discontinued`, `pending`, `mark_as_sold`, `mark_as_expired`.
- Public condition values: `new`, `refurbished`, `used`, `used_like_new`, `used_good`, `used_fair`, `cpo`, `open_box_new`.
- Public visibility values: `published`, `hidden`.
- Invalid items are rejected individually. Valid results preserve submission order, and duplicated retailer IDs are rejected.
- Split oversized updates across calls. Empty and oversized batches fail before execution.
- `SOURCE_MAY_OVERWRITE`: the listed feed or partner platform also supplies the item, and its next update may undo this change. Warn the user in bold.

## Timeouts:
- If a call times out or fails with a server error and returns no result, some items may already have been applied. Retry the same items in smaller calls of about half the previous batch size. Retrying is safe: already-deleted items return `UNKNOWN_RETAILER_ID` rejections, creates upsert, and updates reapply the same values.

## Shared resources:
Fetch via resources/read: `catalog://product-write-fields`, `catalog://id-conventions`, `catalog://errors`.

The current synchronous per-call cap is 25.

tools.name: ads_catalog_update_product_feed
tools.description:
Update settings on an existing product feed (a "data source") under a catalog. This is the "edit feed" counterpart to ads_catalog_create_product_feed. Only the fields you provide are changed; omitted fields are left as-is.

## When to use:
- Rename a feed; change parsing/format (delimiter, encoding, quoted_fields_mode) or default currency.
- Change the recurring fetch schedule / source URL (`replace_schedule`) or incremental update schedule (`update_schedule`).
- Stop/pause automatic refreshing WITHOUT deleting: `clear_replace_schedule` and/or `clear_update_schedule` (feed + ingested products kept). Do NOT delete the feed for this.

## When NOT to use:
- New feed → `ads_catalog_create_product_feed`; immediate refresh → `ads_catalog_create_product_feed_upload_session`; transformation rules → `ads_catalog_create_feed_rule`; inspect only → `ads_catalog_list_product_feeds`.

## Schedule rules:
- `replace_schedule` and `update_schedule` are independent. Within a schedule, "interval" is required, "url" optional (omit to keep existing URL, change timing). (S)FTP needs username/password. Example: `{"interval":"DAILY","hour":6,"url":"https://example.com/feed.csv"}`.
- To stop a schedule set the clear_* flag instead of a schedule object (safe no-op if absent). clear_replace_schedule can't combine with replace_schedule (same for update).

## Shared resources:
Fetch via resources/read: `catalog://id-conventions`, `catalog://errors`.

product_feed_id.description: The ID of the product feed to update (numeric string).

name.description: New human-readable name for the product feed (e.g. "Summer 2026 Catalog Feed"). Omit to leave the name unchanged.

default_currency.description: New ISO 4217 currency code used for items in the feed that do not specify their own currency (e.g. "USD", "GBP"). Omit to leave the default currency unchanged.

delimiter.description: Column delimiter used when parsing CSV/TSV feed files. Use "autodetect" to let Meta infer it. Omit to leave the delimiter unchanged.

encoding.description: Character encoding used when parsing the feed file (e.g. "UTF-8"). Use "autodetect" to let Meta infer it. Omit to leave the encoding unchanged.

quoted_fields_mode.description: Whether feed fields are wrapped in quotes: "on", "off", or "autodetect". Omit to leave this setting unchanged.

replace_schedule.description: New recurring schedule for fully re-fetching the feed from a URL (REPLACE). When provided, it replaces the feed's existing fetch schedule. "interval" is required; omit "url" to keep the current source URL. "DAILY" requires "hour"; "WEEKLY" requires "hour" and "day_of_week"; "MONTHLY" requires "hour" and "day_of_month"; "HOURLY" requires none of these timing fields. Omit the whole object to leave the fetch schedule unchanged. Example: {"interval":"DAILY","hour":6,"url":"https://example.com/feed.csv"}.

interval_count.description: Optional multiplier for interval (1-255, default 1; e.g. every N days).

minute.description: Optional minute of the hour (0-59) to fetch. Defaults to 0 for "DAILY", "WEEKLY", and "MONTHLY", and to the current minute for "HOURLY".

day_of_week.description: Day of week to fetch (e.g. "MONDAY"). Required for "WEEKLY" and not used by other intervals.

day_of_month.description: Day of month to fetch (1-31). Required for "MONTHLY" and not used by other intervals.

timezone.description: Timezone for the schedule (e.g. "America/Los_Angeles"; defaults to America/Los_Angeles).

"interval" is required; omit "url" to keep the current source URL. "DAILY" requires "hour"; "WEEKLY" requires "hour" and "day_of_week"; "MONTHLY" requires "hour" and "day_of_month"; "HOURLY" requires none of these timing fields. Omit the whole object to leave the update schedule unchanged. Example: {"interval":"DAILY","hour":6,"url":"https://example.com/feed.csv"}.

timezone.description: Timezone for the schedule (e.g. "America/Los_Angeles"; defaults to America/Los_Angeles).

The feed and its already-ingested products are kept. Use this (not ads_catalog_product_feed_delete) when the advertiser wants to pause/stop/turn off automatic refreshing. Mutually exclusive with "replace_schedule".

tools.name: ads_create_ad
tools.description:
Creates a single ad under an existing ad set in PAUSED state. There is no status input: to make the ad live, create it, then call ads_activate_entity on it.

DRAFT MODE: Draft mode is enabled for you, so this tool does NOT create a live ad. It stages the ad in the account's Ads Manager draft under the given ad set and returns status=DRAFT with the allocated ad_id. Nothing is created until you publish that campaign with ads_activate_entity on the campaign; published objects go live ACTIVE. Any validation errors are surfaced in active_errors.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID. Format: numeric ID without "act_" prefix.

ad_set_id.description: The ad set ID to create the ad under.

creative.description: JSON string of creative spec. A live ad requires this, including when source_ad_id is set. In draft mode, source_ad_id copies the source ad's creative when this field is omitted. Explicitly passing the source ad's creative is safe in both modes and prevents live calls from being rejected. To duplicate an ad, pass the source ad's creative as {"creative_id":"<CREATIVE_ID>"} (read it with ads_get_ad_entities). It MUST include exactly one creative source: (a) creative_id — reuse an existing creative entity; (b) object_story_id — promote an existing post, format "pageID_postID"; (c) object_story_spec — inline creative; the spec MUST contain page_id (use ads_get_pages_for_business to find valid Page IDs) plus one of link_data, video_data, photo_data, or template_data; (d) source_instagram_media_id — promote an existing ORGANIC Instagram post: pass an `id` returned by ads_get_ig_media for the ad's Instagram account; ad IDs, creative IDs and ad copies (boosted or dark posts) are rejected; (e) asset_feed_spec — dynamic creative with multiple assets. SETUP COMPATIBILITY: the creative must match the parent ad set's destination and optimization goal and the campaign objective. For LINK_CLICKS, use a creative with a valid external destination and a real CTA button; an existing post that links only to Facebook or has no CTA is incompatible. Create an inline/link creative with link_url plus call_to_action_type instead of retrying that post. EXISTING POST LIFECYCLE: object_story_id must name a post that still exists, is published, belongs to the stated Page, and is visible/promotable by the caller. A deleted, unpublished, or inaccessible post cannot be repaired by retrying; choose a current post or create an inline creative. New inline creatives default top-level contextual_multi_ads.enroll_status to OPT_OUT. Set it to OPT_IN only when the advertiser explicitly opts in. This setting cannot be changed when the request reuses an existing creative, Facebook post, or Instagram post through creative_id, object_story_id, or source_instagram_media_id. CRITICAL: page_id is ALWAYS required inside object_story_spec — omitting it causes "Facebook Page is Missing" rejection. For Placement Asset Customization, first call ads_create_creative with placement_customizations, then pass {"creative_id":"<CREATIVE_ID>"} here. Do not rebuild that creative through this inline object_story_spec path. For multi-media optimization, first call ads_create_creative with multi_media, then pass its creative_id here. Do not pass a raw media_sourcing_spec through this inline creative path. FIELD PLACEMENT: For link_data, prefer image_hash (from ads_get_ad_images) over image_url; image_hash references an already-uploaded image and is the canonical field. If you have only an image URL, place it at the creative top level (not inside link_data). VIDEO THUMBNAIL: video_data REQUIRES a thumbnail — set one of image_hash or image_url inside video_data. Omitting both is rejected with "Your ad needs a video thumbnail: Please specify one of image_hash or image_url in the video_data". VIDEO CTA: when video_data sets link_description, it MUST also set a call_to_action, or the request is rejected with "Ad creative's video_data requires call_to_action to set link_description". MULTI-DESTINATION: a creative that sends people to more than one destination (e.g. a click-to-message multi-destination ad, or an asset_feed_spec with multiple destinations) MUST include a degrees_of_freedom_spec that declares the multi-destination optimization. Omitting it is rejected with "Creative is missing DOF spec: Creative should have degrees_of_freedom spec for multi-destination ads". A single-destination creative does not need it. ADVANTAGE+ CREATIVE: Set feature enrollments inside degrees_of_freedom_spec.creative_features_spec as {"<feature>":{"enroll_status":"OPT_IN"|"OPT_OUT"}}. Use image_animation for the Image Animation enhancement. Do not set standard_enhancements: Marketing API creation rejects the field even when it is OPT_OUT. Do not set cv_transformation: it is 3D Animation, which is only available to ads created in Ads Manager. When source_ad_id is supplied with a new object_story_spec creative, compatible source feature state may be inherited; source_feature_inheritance in the response reports whether it was. An explicit feature entry in this creative replaces the inherited entry. Set other opt-ins (e.g. image_touchups) only after confirming the new creative is eligible. Minimal example: {"object_story_spec":{"page_id":"<PAGE_ID>","link_data":{"link":"https://example.com","image_hash":"<HASH>","message":"Check this out"}}}

Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

tools.name: ads_create_ad_set
tools.description:
Creates a single ad set under an existing campaign in PAUSED state.

  BEFORE CALLING: The `ads_create_campaign` response includes `valid_optimization_goals` and `recommended_optimization_goal` for the campaign's objective. Use ONLY values from that list for `optimization_goal`. A goal outside that list is replaced with the recommended default at the server, but a goal on the list can still be rejected for its `destination_type`, `promoted_object`, or `billing_event`; follow the pairings on those parameters.

  TARGETING — META RECOMMENDS ADVANTAGE+ AUDIENCE: Keep Advantage+ Audience (A+A) on wherever the ad set supports it. Omit `targeting_automation` (the server enables A+A) or send `targeting_automation.advantage_audience` = 1. Under A+A, Meta's delivery system finds the audience most likely to convert and uses the advertiser's targeting as suggestions: `age_min`/`age_max`, `genders`, interests and behaviors, custom audiences and lookalikes. Locations, `excluded_custom_audiences`, languages and `age_min` up to 25 stay hard controls. Pass ages as-is: the server sends them as suggestions under `targeting_automation.advantage_audience`, so `age_max` stops being a hard cap and `age_min` stays a hard minimum clamped to 18-25 (send at least 20 when targeting Thailand). A target-customer description ("women 25-45"), an age range, an `age_max` of 65, interests, or a custom audience is NOT a reason to turn A+A off. Set `targeting_automation.advantage_audience` = 0 ONLY when the advertiser explicitly asks to turn Advantage+ Audience off, requires an age limit A+A cannot enforce (a hard maximum below 65 or a hard minimum above 25), or requires delivery to ONLY the people in a custom audience; then tell them A+A is off and why. For HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT or FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES campaigns, the special ad category age rules on `targeting` take precedence.

  TARGETING — INTERESTS: Do NOT invent interest IDs. Omit interests and use broad targeting via `geo_locations` (recommended); only include interest IDs the user has explicitly provided.

  PLACEMENTS: Advantage+ placements is the default when the advertiser did not specify placements. Honor an explicit restriction by putting `publisher_platforms` and the matching position arrays inside `targeting`; omit all placement fields for Advantage+ placements. Never claim that placements were selected unless those fields were sent.

  LEAD ADS: When `optimization_goal` is `LEAD_GENERATION` or `QUALITY_LEAD`, the Page in `promoted_object.page_id` must have `leadgen_tos_accepted=true` — check the page list returned by `ads_get_ad_account_pages`. If the user's page has not accepted ToS, instruct them to do so at https://www.facebook.com/legal/leadgen/tos before creating the ad set.

  MESSAGING DESTINATIONS: When `destination_type` is `WHATSAPP`, `MESSENGER`, or `INSTAGRAM_DIRECT`, `promoted_object.page_id` is required. If omitted, the tool auto-infers it from the ad account's primary promoted Page.

  PROFILE VISIT ADS: pair `OUTCOME_TRAFFIC` with `optimization_goal=PROFILE_VISIT` or `OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT` with `optimization_goal=PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT`. Set `destination_type` to `INSTAGRAM_PROFILE` or `FACEBOOK_PAGE` for single-destination, or `INSTAGRAM_PROFILE_AND_FACEBOOK_PAGE` for multi-destination.

  EU / DSA: When `geo_locations.countries` includes any EU country, `dsa_beneficiary` and `dsa_payor` are required for Digital Services Act compliance. If omitted, both are auto-filled from the ad account's business name; provide them explicitly to override.

  BUDGET: Read `min_daily_budget_cents` from `ads_get_ad_accounts` before setting `daily_budget` — budgets below the per-currency minimum are rejected. Before setting an ad-set budget, call `ads_get_ad_entities` for the parent campaign and request its budget fields. If it has a campaign-level budget, leave `daily_budget` and `lifetime_budget` unset. All budget values are in the smallest unit of the ad account's `currency` (e.g., cents for USD). `daily_budget` and `lifetime_budget` are not interchangeable. Use one only when the advertiser states that cadence. A periodic amount such as "$2,000/month" is neither; if unclear, ask and wait instead of choosing one.

  ADVANTAGE+ CATALOG / DYNAMIC ADS: When the creative (attached at ad creation) is catalog-backed — `ads_create_creative` with `product_set_id` — check the catalog supporting it is healthy: use `ads_catalog_get_diagnostics` and `ads_catalog_get_dynamic_ads_health` to surface feed, data-source, or product-set issues that would prevent the ad set from delivering, and `ads_catalog_list_products` / `ads_catalog_list_product_sets` to verify the product set is non-empty.

DRAFT MODE: Draft mode is enabled for you, so this tool does NOT create a live ad set. It stages the ad set in your draft under the given campaign and returns status=DRAFT with the allocated ad_set_id. Nothing is created until you publish the whole draft with ads_activate_entity on the campaign; published objects go live ACTIVE. Any validation errors are surfaced in active_errors.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID. Format: numeric ID without "act_" prefix.

campaign_id.description: The campaign ID to create the ad set under.

billing_event.description: What the advertiser is charged for. Use IMPRESSIONS, which is valid for every optimization_goal. Other billing events are goal-specific: for example, LINK_CLICKS pairs with optimization_goal=LINK_CLICKS, THRUPLAY with THRUPLAY, and PAGE_LIKES with PAGE_LIKES. Invalid pairings are rejected.

optimization_goal.description:
What the ad set is optimized for. Pick the value whose human label matches the user's intent — do NOT guess. Supported values: REACH (Reach), IMPRESSIONS (Impressions), LINK_CLICKS (Link Clicks), LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS (Landing Page Views), ENGAGED_PAGE_VIEWS (Engaged Page Views — users who stay on the landing page), POST_ENGAGEMENT (Post Engagement), PAGE_LIKES (Page Likes), EVENT_RESPONSES (Event Responses), OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS (Conversions / Purchases / Add to Cart), VALUE (Conversion Value / ROAS), LEAD_GENERATION (Leads), QUALITY_LEAD (Conversion Leads), CONVERSATIONS (Conversations), MESSAGING_PURCHASE_CONVERSION (Messaging Purchases — optimize for purchases in messaging conversations; pair with a messaging destination_type such as MESSENGER, WHATSAPP, or INSTAGRAM_DIRECT), QUALITY_CALL (Calls), MEANINGFUL_CALL_ATTEMPT (Meaningful Calls — optimize for call attempts initiated through messaging), APP_INSTALLS (App Installs), IN_APP_VALUE (In-App Value — optimize for in-app purchase value in app promotion campaigns), THRUPLAY (ThruPlay), TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS (2-second continuous video plays), VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE (Instagram profile visits — pair with destination_type=INSTAGRAM_PROFILE), PROFILE_VISIT (profile visits — pair with destination_type=FACEBOOK_PAGE for "Maximize Facebook Page visits" or destination_type=INSTAGRAM_PROFILE for IG profile visits), PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT (Profile and Page Engagement — unified profile/page visit optimization; pair with destination_type=INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, FACEBOOK_PAGE, or INSTAGRAM_PROFILE_AND_FACEBOOK_PAGE), REMINDERS_SET (Reminders set), AD_RECALL_LIFT (Ad Recall Lift). Some goals are gated per-account (e.g. MESSAGING_PURCHASE_CONVERSION, MEANINGFUL_CALL_ATTEMPT, IN_APP_VALUE, ENGAGED_PAGE_VIEWS) — the Marketing API returns an error if the account is not eligible. Compatibility with the parent campaign's objective is enforced by the Marketing API. 

  OBJECTIVE → COMPATIBLE optimization_goal VALUES (default listed first; pick from this list based on the parent campaign's objective — values outside the list are rejected with "Performance goal isn't available with this objective"): OUTCOME_AWARENESS → REACH (default), IMPRESSIONS, AD_RECALL_LIFT, THRUPLAY, TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS. OUTCOME_TRAFFIC → LINK_CLICKS (default), LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, IMPRESSIONS, POST_ENGAGEMENT, REACH, CONVERSATIONS, THRUPLAY, VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, PROFILE_VISIT, QUALITY_CALL, REMINDERS_SET. OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT → THRUPLAY (default), POST_ENGAGEMENT, EVENT_RESPONSES, PAGE_LIKES, IMPRESSIONS, REACH, TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS, LINK_CLICKS, CONVERSATIONS, OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, QUALITY_CALL. OUTCOME_LEADS → OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS (default), LEAD_GENERATION, QUALITY_LEAD, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, LINK_CLICKS, IMPRESSIONS, REACH, VALUE, CONVERSATIONS (WHATSAPP destination only), QUALITY_CALL. OUTCOME_SALES → OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS (default), VALUE, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, IMPRESSIONS, POST_ENGAGEMENT, REACH, LINK_CLICKS, CONVERSATIONS. OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION → APP_INSTALLS (default), OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, IMPRESSIONS, LINK_CLICKS, REACH, VALUE. VIDEO_VIEWS (10-second views) is deprecated under every objective; use THRUPLAY. Account-gated goals that may also be valid for specific objectives: ENGAGED_PAGE_VIEWS (Traffic), MEANINGFUL_CALL_ATTEMPT (Traffic, Engagement), MESSAGING_PURCHASE_CONVERSION (Engagement, Sales — messaging destinations only), IN_APP_VALUE (App Promotion). When in doubt, pick the default (first value listed).

targeting.description: JSON string of targeting spec. IMPORTANT: Do NOT invent interest IDs — interest targeting requires real numeric IDs from the Facebook Targeting Search API (typically 13–16 digit numbers like "6003139266461"). If you do not have valid interest IDs, use geo_locations-only broad targeting instead. Example (broad, recommended when interest IDs are unknown): {"geo_locations":{"countries":["US"]}}. Advantage+ Audience is on by default; do NOT add "targeting_automation":{"advantage_audience":0} unless the tool description's conditions for turning it off are met. Manual placements go in this same object. For Facebook Feed and Instagram Reels only, use {"geo_locations":{"countries":["US"]},"publisher_platforms":["facebook","instagram"],"facebook_positions":["feed"],"instagram_positions":["reels"]}. For Advantage+ placements, omit `publisher_platforms` and every `*_positions` field. Example (with verified interest): {"geo_locations":{"countries":["US"]},"flexible_spec":[{"interests":[{"id":"6003139266461","name":"Movies"}]}]}. Never use placeholder IDs like "000" or "123" — they will be rejected. SPECIAL AD CATEGORIES: when the parent campaign is HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT or FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES, give every city, address or custom location a `radius` and `distance_unit` of at least 15 miles (25 km), whatever country is targeted; this meets the minimum in every region.
