Never use `zips`, `subcities`, `neighborhoods`, `subneighborhoods`, `metro_areas`, `small_geo_areas`, `electoral_districts` or `political_districts` in `geo_locations`. Every country targeted by `geo_locations` must appear in the parent campaign's `special_ad_category_country`; territories of those countries are also allowed. Keep `age_min` at 18 and `age_max` at 65, and do not add interests or other detailed targeting. `countries` and `regions` need no radius.

daily_budget.description: ONLY WHEN PARENT CAMPAIGN HAS NO BUDGET (ABO mode). Daily budget in cents. Only set this when the parent campaign does NOT use CBO (i.e., has no campaign_daily_budget or campaign_lifetime_budget). Mutually exclusive with lifetime_budget. IMPORTANT: If the user has not explicitly requested ABO, prefer setting campaign_daily_budget on the campaign instead (CBO is recommended). If neither budget is set here and the parent is not CBO, the tool will ask you to choose CBO or ABO explicitly.

lifetime_budget.description: ONLY WHEN PARENT CAMPAIGN HAS NO BUDGET (ABO mode). Lifetime budget in cents. Only set this when the parent campaign does NOT use CBO. Mutually exclusive with daily_budget. Requires end_time. Prefer setting campaign_lifetime_budget on the campaign instead (CBO is recommended).

start_time.description: Optional. Ad set start time in ISO 8601 format.

end_time.description: Optional. Ad set end time in ISO 8601 format. Required when using lifetime_budget.

bid_strategy.description: ABO ONLY — do NOT pass under a CBO parent campaign (one that has campaign_daily_budget or campaign_lifetime_budget set); the campaign-level bid strategy governs all child ad sets and the API rejects ad-set-level bidding with "Must Use Campaign Bid Strategy". Optional. Ad set bid strategy. Values: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP (default — automatic bidding, no bid_amount needed), LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP (REQUIRES bid_amount — sets a maximum bid cap in cents), COST_CAP (REQUIRES bid_amount — sets an average cost-per-result target in cents), LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS (for value optimization — requires bid_constraints with roas_average_floor). If omitted, defaults to LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP (autobid).

bid_amount.description: ABO ONLY — do NOT pass under a CBO parent. Bid cap or cost target in cents. REQUIRED when bid_strategy is LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP or COST_CAP. Not needed for LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP (autobid).

promoted_object.description: REQUIRED when optimization_goal is OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, VALUE, LEAD_GENERATION, QUALITY_LEAD, APP_INSTALLS, or IN_APP_VALUE — the Marketing API rejects without it. Optional for other goals (REACH, IMPRESSIONS, LINK_CLICKS, etc.). JSON string of promoted object spec — usually a pixel, app, page, or custom event. REQUIRED for OUTCOME_SALES campaigns with WEBSITE destination: without a promoted_object containing a pixel_id, the Marketing API rejects the create with "Performance goal isn't available" because no optimization goals are valid for that combination. Strongly recommended for conversion-tracking goals (OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS, VALUE) under OUTCOME_LEADS as well. For OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, promoted_object is optional. Format examples: {"pixel_id":"123"} (website conversions / landing page views), {"pixel_id":"123","custom_event_type":"PURCHASE"} (specific event), {"custom_conversion_id":"123"} (custom conversion), {"application_id":"123","object_store_url":"..."} (app installs), {"page_id":"123"} (page-related goals; under OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT also set destination_type, see that parameter), {"pixel_id":"123","custom_event_type":"PURCHASE","custom_attribution_source_ids":["456"]} (Custom Attribution / passback — optimizes toward an external Source-of-Truth attribution source. Requires an OUTCOME_SALES campaign, an OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS or VALUE goal, LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP bidding and a PURCHASE event. Incremental attribution must be disabled, and value_rule_set_id must not be set. Supported promoted object types are PIXEL (website-only), WEB_AND_APP, and PRODUCT_SET; MOBILE_APP (app-only) is not supported. Use one source id for website-only. Up to two are allowed for website+app, or for a catalog product set with both web and app sources: list the web/pixel CAS first and the app CAS second. A single CAS can cover website+app when its pixel dataset already has a linked app. A source id is NOT a pixel or dataset id — it comes from Events Manager > Settings > Custom attribution source. Settable only when the ad set is created).

destination_type.description: REQUIRED for messaging and profile goals — see below. Where the ad drives people. Values: WEBSITE, APP, MESSENGER, INSTAGRAM_DIRECT, WHATSAPP, PHONE_CALL, ON_AD, ON_EVENT, ON_PAGE, ON_POST, ON_VIDEO, INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, FACEBOOK_PAGE, INSTAGRAM_PROFILE_AND_FACEBOOK_PAGE, LEAD_FORM_MESSENGER. REQUIRED pairings: CONVERSATIONS / MESSAGING_PURCHASE_CONVERSION / MEANINGFUL_CALL_ATTEMPT → MESSENGER, WHATSAPP, or INSTAGRAM_DIRECT (under OUTCOME_LEADS, CONVERSATIONS needs WHATSAPP; MESSENGER there supports only LEAD_GENERATION). Under OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT with a promoted_object: POST_ENGAGEMENT → ON_POST, PAGE_LIKES → ON_PAGE, THRUPLAY / TWO_SECOND_CONTINUOUS_VIDEO_VIEWS → ON_VIDEO; without a destination those goals are rejected with "Performance goal isn't available". VISIT_INSTAGRAM_PROFILE → INSTAGRAM_PROFILE. PROFILE_VISIT → FACEBOOK_PAGE or INSTAGRAM_PROFILE. PROFILE_AND_PAGE_ENGAGEMENT → INSTAGRAM_PROFILE, FACEBOOK_PAGE, or INSTAGRAM_PROFILE_AND_FACEBOOK_PAGE. WEBSITE is the typical pairing for LANDING_PAGE_VIEWS / OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS / VALUE goals.

adset_schedule.description: Optional. JSON array of day-parting schedule objects. Example: [{"start_minute":0,"end_minute":1440,"days":[0,1,2,3,4,5,6]}]

pacing_type.description: Optional. JSON array of pacing type. Values: ["standard"], ["day_parting"], ["no_pacing"].

attribution_spec.description: Optional. JSON array of attribution spec for conversion tracking. RECOMMENDED: omit this field unless the advertiser explicitly requests a specific window. Default: 7-day click-through + 1-day view-through. Override example (7-day click only): [{"event_type":"CLICK_THROUGH","window_days":7}]. Valid event_types: CLICK_THROUGH, VIEW_THROUGH, ENGAGED_VIDEO_VIEW.

frequency_control_specs.description: Optional. JSON array of frequency capping specs.

is_dynamic_creative.description: Optional. Whether this ad set uses dynamic creative optimization.

existing_customer_budget_percentage.description: Optional. Budget percentage for existing customers (Advantage+ shopping).

tune_for_category.description: Optional. Special ad category tuning. Values: HOUSING, EMPLOYMENT, FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES, ISSUES_ELECTIONS_POLITICS.

bid_constraints.description: ABO ONLY — do NOT pass under a CBO parent (bidding lives on the campaign in that case). REQUIRED when bid_strategy is LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS. JSON object with roas_average_floor (minimum ROAS as percentage, e.g. {"roas_average_floor":200} = 2.00x). Not needed for other bid strategies.

optimization_sub_event.description: Optional. Sub-event for optimization (e.g., specific app event).

multi_optimization_goal_weight.description: Optional. Weight for multi-optimization goal. Values: UNDEFINED, BALANCED, PREFER_EVENT.

daily_min_spend_target.description: Optional. Minimum daily spend target in cents.

daily_spend_cap.description: Optional. Daily spend cap in cents.

lifetime_min_spend_target.description: Optional. Minimum lifetime spend target in cents.

lifetime_spend_cap.description: Optional. Lifetime spend cap in cents.

dsa_beneficiary.description: Optional. Digital Services Act beneficiary name.

dsa_payor.description: Optional. Digital Services Act payor name.

campaign_attribution.description: Optional. Attribution type for app campaigns. Values: AEM, SKAN.

is_incremental_attribution_enabled.description: Optional. Whether the campaign should use incremental attribution optimization. Incremental attribution is an attribution model that optimizes ad delivery for incremental conversions. It uses machine learning models that predict whether a conversion is caused by an ad. Supported bid strategies are: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP, COST_CAP, and LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS (autobid campaigns are always allowed). Supported optimization goals are: OFFSITE_CONVERSIONS, VALUE, and RETURN_ON_AD_SPEND. Supported promoted object types are: PIXEL, WEBSITE, PRODUCT_SET, WEB_AND_APP, and WEB_AND_SHOP (plus WEBSITE_AND_IN_STORE and WEBSITE_APP_AND_IN_STORE for accounts gated into omni/web-app-instore). For value-optimized goals (VALUE, ROAS), the supported promoted object semantic value types are: VALUE, MARGIN, and LIFETIME_VALUE. When using incremental attribution you should not provide a value for `attribution_spec`.

adlabels.description: Optional. JSON array of ad label specs. Example: [{"name":"My Label"}]

budget_schedule_specs.description: Optional. JSON array of budget schedule specs for high demand periods. Each spec has time_start, time_end, budget_value, budget_value_type.

budget_source.description: Optional. Budget source. Values: NONE, RMN.

budget_split_set_id.description: Optional. Budget split set ID as numeric string.

daily_imps.description: Optional. Daily impressions. Only for campaigns with buying_type=FIXED_CPM.

lifetime_imps.description: Optional. Lifetime impressions. Only for campaigns with buying_type=FIXED_CPM.

io_number.description: Optional. Insertion order number for direct deals.

cost_bidding_mode.description: Optional. Cost bidding mode. Values: VOLUME_FOCUSED, BALANCED, COST_FOCUSED.

campaign_spec.description: Optional. JSON object of campaign spec with name, objective, and buying_type for inline campaign creation.

campaign_active_time.description: Optional. Campaign active time as a UNIX timestamp (seconds since epoch).

campaign_targeting_consolidation.description: Optional. Campaign targeting consolidation phase. Values: PHASE_1, PHASE_2, PHASE_3.

source_adset_id.description: Optional. Source ad set ID to copy from, as numeric string.

split_test_config_splits_index.description: Optional. Index for the splits vector from split test config on the parent campaign.

automatic_manual_state.description: Optional. Automatic/manual state. Values: UNSET, AUTOMATIC, MANUAL.

calling_settings.description: Optional. JSON object of calling settings for call-based ads.

naming_template_custom_fields.description: Optional. JSON object of naming template custom fields for ad set naming conventions.

marketing_goal.description: Optional. Marketing goal. Values: NONE, NEW_CUSTOMER_ACQUISITION.

biz_ai_enabled_state.description: Optional. Business AI enabled state. Values: APP_ONBOARDING_REQUIRED, APP_ONBOARDING_STARTED, APP_ONBOARDING_NOT_REQUIRED, OPT_OUT_ONBOARDING, ONBOARDED_AI_REPLY_ON, ONBOARDED_AI_REPLY_OFF, NOT_ENABLED, CURRENT_CAMPAIGN_ONLY, ALL_CAMPAIGNS.

saved_audience.description: Optional. JSON object of saved audience spec including targeting, name, and other audience configuration.

saved_audience_id.description: Optional. Saved audience ID as numeric string.

targeting_as_signal.description: Optional. Indicates if campaign is using targeting criteria as a signal.

adjust_lookalikes.description: Optional. Whether to adjust lookalike audiences.

brand_audience_id.description: Optional. Brand audience ID as numeric string.

reporting_audience.description: Optional. JSON object of reporting audience spec for cross-account reporting.

placement.description: Optional advanced placement spec. For ordinary manual placement selection, use `publisher_platforms` and the matching `*_positions` fields inside `targeting`; do not send the same restriction in both fields.

placement_soft_opt_out.description: Optional. JSON object of placement soft opt-out spec to exclude specific placements without hard constraints.

rf_prediction_id.description: Optional. Reach and frequency prediction ID as numeric string.

contextual_bundling_spec.description: Optional. JSON object of contextual bundling spec for ads in Facebook contextual surfaces.

creative_sequence.description: Optional. JSON array of ad group IDs defining the sequence to show to users.

creative_diversity_data.description: Optional. JSON object of creative diversity data including scores and labels for creative variation analysis.

creative_diversity_label.description: Optional. Creative diversity label. Values: HIGH, LOW, MEDIUM.

creative_diversity_score.description: Optional. Creative diversity score (0.0-1.0) measuring variation across ad creatives.

creative_fatigue_prediction_ple.description: Optional. JSON object of creative fatigue prediction PLE data.

is_dynamic_creative_format_automation.description: Optional. Whether to use dynamic creative format automation.

is_dynamic_creative_optimization.description: Optional. Whether to use dynamic creative optimization. Deprecated in v3.2.

multi_event_conversion_attribution_windo.description: Optional. Multi-event conversion attribution window in seconds.

low_creative_reach.description: Optional. Low creative reach indicator. Values: HIGH, LOW, MEDIUM.

conversion_goal_id.description: Optional. ID of the conversion goal (CSA) as numeric string.

conversion_locations.description: Optional; usually omit, since destination_type already sets where conversions happen. Common values: WEBSITE, MOBILE_APP, WEB_AND_APP, MESSENGER, WHATSAPP, INSTAGRAM_DIRECT, PHONE_CALL, WEBSITE_AND_PHONE_CALL.

conversion_value_expression_spec.description: Optional. JSON array of conversion value expression specs.

partnership_ad_content_lists.description: Optional. JSON array of partnership ad content lists.

shops_ads_metadata_tags.description: Optional. JSON array of shops ads metadata tag integers.

is_message_marketing.description: Optional. Whether this is message marketing.

time_based_ad_rotation_id_blocks.description: Optional. JSON array of arrays of ad group IDs for time-based ad rotation.

time_based_ad_rotation_intervals.description: Optional. JSON array of UNIX timestamps defining date ranges for ad rotation.

time_start.description: Optional. Time start in ISO 8601 format or UNIX timestamp.

time_stop.description: Optional. Time stop in ISO 8601 format or UNIX timestamp.

time_suggestion.description: Optional. JSON object of suggested start/stop time for the ad set based on delivery optimization.

include_in_ad_study_cell_id.description: Optional. Ad study cell ID to include this ad set in, as numeric string.

include_in_ad_study_id.description: Optional. Ad study ID to include this ad set in, as numeric string.

lightweight_split_test_options.description: Optional. JSON object of lightweight A/B split test configuration options.

guidance_lift_estimate.description: Optional. JSON object of lift estimation for each guidance object.

brand_safety_config.description: Optional. JSON object of brand safety configuration.

breakdown_effect_eligibility.description: Optional. Whether breakdown effect is eligible.

is_lifetime_flex_with_valid_schedule.description: Optional. Whether the campaign is lifetime flex with a valid schedule.

is_sac_cfca_terms_certified.description: Optional. Whether SAC CFCA terms are certified.

metrics_metadata.description: Optional. JSON object of metrics metadata related to this ad set.

relative_value.description: Optional. Relative value weight (0.0-1.0) for multi-optimization goal balancing.

value_rule_set_id.description: Optional. Value rule set ID as numeric string.

value_rules_applied.description: Optional. Whether value rules are applied.

value_rules_spec.description: Optional. JSON object of value rules spec.

hide_ui.description: Optional. Set to true when creating many ad objects at once to avoid showing too many UI widgets, or when the user asks to hide the UI.

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

tools.name: ads_create_campaign
tools.description:
Creates a single campaign (campaign group) in PAUSED state. Use this to create just a campaign without an ad set or ad. 

  BUDGET PLACEMENT — DEFAULT TO CBO: Unless the advertiser explicitly requests ad-set-level budgeting (ABO), put their stated budget at campaign level (CBO). CBO controls where the budget is allocated; it does not determine the amount or cadence. 

  BUDGET AMOUNT AND CADENCE — DO NOT INFER: Set campaign_daily_budget only when the advertiser states a daily amount, and campaign_lifetime_budget only when they state a total campaign budget. Pass every budget value in the ad account currency's smallest unit (for example, cents for USD). A periodic amount such as "$2,000/month" is neither. If the amount or cadence is unclear, ask and wait before calling this tool; do not stage an assumed value for confirmation. 

  CBO (Campaign Budget Optimization): Pass campaign_daily_budget OR campaign_lifetime_budget here. campaign_bid_strategy defaults to LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP if omitted; pass it explicitly for COST_CAP, LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, or LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS. ABO (Ad Set Budget Optimization): Leave campaign_daily_budget, campaign_lifetime_budget, AND campaign_bid_strategy unset on this call, then pass daily_budget / lifetime_budget on the subsequent ads_create_ad_set call. Only use ABO if the advertiser specifically asks to control budget per ad set. Setting any campaign-level budget field implicitly switches the campaign to CBO; if the advertiser asked for ABO, do NOT set them. 

  ENFORCED: ads_create_ad_set pre-validates this and will reject calls that pass daily_budget or lifetime_budget under a CBO parent campaign.

  VERIFY THE RESULT: After a successful create, call `ads_get_ad_entities` with the returned campaign ID in `object_ids`, `level=campaign`, and `fields` containing the changed fields plus `effective_status`. Report the returned values to the advertiser. 

  POTENTIAL NEXT STEP — RECOMMEND OPPORTUNITY SCORE: After verifying the campaign, suggest calling `ads_get_opportunity_score` with the ad account ID to check whether the account follows Meta best practices and to get personalized recommendations that can improve performance.

DRAFT MODE: Draft mode is enabled for you, so this tool does NOT create a live campaign. It stages the campaign in the account's Ads Manager draft (visible/editable in Ads Manager) and returns status=DRAFT with the allocated campaign_id. The draft may already contain other campaigns; this adds one more. Nothing is created until you publish: add an ad set (ads_create_ad_set) and an ad (ads_create_ad) under it, then call ads_activate_entity on the campaign to publish that campaign (its ad set and ad). Published objects go live ACTIVE (publishing is the advertiser's go-live intent), so there is no separate activate-after-publish step. Any staged object's validation errors are surfaced in active_errors.

ad_account_id.description: The ad account ID. Format: numeric ID without "act_" prefix.

objective.description: Campaign objective. Only ODAX outcome values are accepted: OUTCOME_AWARENESS, OUTCOME_TRAFFIC, OUTCOME_ENGAGEMENT, OUTCOME_LEADS, OUTCOME_SALES, OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION. Legacy objectives (APP_INSTALLS, BRAND_AWARENESS, REACH, LEAD_GENERATION, LINK_CLICKS, VIDEO_VIEWS, etc.) are not supported and the request fails with VALIDATION. Map APP_INSTALLS to OUTCOME_APP_PROMOTION.

buying_type.description: Campaign buying type. Values: AUCTION (default), RESERVED.

special_ad_categories.description: JSON array of special ad categories. Defaults to "[]". Values: NONE, EMPLOYMENT, HOUSING, FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES, ISSUES_ELECTIONS_POLITICS, ONLINE_GAMBLING_AND_GAMING. HOUSING also covers mortgages and other home loans. CREDIT is retired: use FINANCIAL_PRODUCTS_SERVICES for other credit, loans, insurance and financial products. Use these exact values, not display names.

campaign_bid_strategy.description: CBO ONLY. Campaign-level bid strategy. Defaults to LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP if omitted (recommended for "highest volume" or "lowest cost" strategies). Set explicitly for other strategies. Values: LOWEST_COST_WITHOUT_CAP, LOWEST_COST_WITH_BID_CAP, COST_CAP, LOWEST_COST_WITH_MIN_ROAS. Do NOT set this field for ABO — set the bid strategy on the ad set instead.

campaign_daily_budget.description: Optional. CBO ONLY. Campaign daily budget in cents. Mutually exclusive with campaign_lifetime_budget. Do NOT set this field for ABO — pass daily_budget on the subsequent ads_create_ad_set call instead.

campaign_lifetime_budget.description: Optional. CBO ONLY. Campaign lifetime budget in cents. Mutually exclusive with campaign_daily_budget. Do NOT set this field for ABO — pass lifetime_budget on the subsequent ads_create_ad_set call instead.

campaign_spend_cap.description: Optional. Maximum total spend cap for the campaign in cents.

campaign_start_time.description: Optional. Campaign start time in ISO 8601 format.

campaign_stop_time.description: Optional. Campaign stop time in ISO 8601 format.

promoted_object.description: Optional. JSON string of promoted object spec. Required for some objectives (APP_PROMOTION, LEADS, etc.).

special_ad_category_country.description: Optional. JSON array of country codes for special ad categories. Example: ["US","CA"]. Every country targeted by an ad set's `geo_locations` must appear in this list; territories of listed countries are also allowed.

is_skadnetwork_attribution.description: Optional. Enable SKAdNetwork attribution for iOS app campaigns.

budget_schedule_specs.description: Optional. JSON array of budget schedule specs for high-demand periods.

adlabels.description: Optional. JSON array of ad label specs. Example: [{"name":"My Label"}]

campaign_optimization_type.description: Optional. Campaign optimization type. Values: NONE, ICO_ONLY.

is_using_l3_schedule.description: Optional. Whether the campaign uses L3 schedule.

iterative_split_test_configs.description: Optional. JSON array of iterative split test configuration specs.

source_campaign_id.description: Optional. The source campaign ID to copy settings from.

topline_id.description: Optional. The topline ID to associate with this campaign.

hide_ui.description: Optional. Set to true when creating many ad objects at once to avoid showing too many UI widgets, or when the user asks to hide the UI.

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

tools.name: ads_create_creative
tools.description:
Creates an ad creative on the specified ad account. Supports eight formats: single-image, single-video, Placement Asset Customization (PAC), multi-media optimization (MMU), Advantage+ catalog carousel, static carousel (manually specified cards), boosted post (an existing organic Page post), Facebook Partnership Ads from existing posts, and Instagram Partnership Ads built from new media.

  ## Required fields by format:

  **Image ads:**
  - `ad_account_id`, `page_id`, `link_url` (`link_url` is not required for click-to-messaging creatives — see below)
  - One of `image_hash` or `image_url` (the ad image; never both)

  **Video ads:**
  - `ad_account_id`, `page_id`, `video_id`
  - `link_url` — optional in general, but REQUIRED if you set `description` (see below), unless `call_to_action_type` is a click-to-messaging CTA
  - One of `image_hash` or `image_url` — required; represents the **video thumbnail** (cover image shown before the video plays; never both)
  - Setting `description` on a video ad also requires `link_url`, unless `call_to_action_type` is a click-to-messaging CTA. `description` maps to `video_data.link_description`, which the backend rejects unless the video has a call to action — and this tool attaches the CTA only when `link_url` is present (button defaults to LEARN_MORE, or `call_to_action_type` if you set one), or when `call_to_action_type` is a click-to-messaging CTA (`WHATSAPP_MESSAGE` / `MESSAGE_PAGE`), which attaches its own button and takes no `link_url`. Any other `call_to_action_type` alone, without `link_url`, does NOT attach a CTA. So to add a video `description`, provide `link_url` (and optionally `call_to_action_type`), or use a click-to-messaging `call_to_action_type` without `link_url`.

  **Product Extensions (catalog products shown beneath the ad's own media):**
  Not available on every single-image or single-video ad. Request it explicitly through `advantage_plus_creative_features` or `degrees_of_freedom_spec`, and supply `objective`, `conversion_location`, and `link_url`; the tool then resolves an eligible catalog product set and keeps the supplied image or video as the main media. Every condition below must hold:
  - Single-image or single-video only. PAC, MMU, carousel, collection, boosted-post, and Partnership Ad creatives are rejected.
  - Campaign setup is `objective` OUTCOME_SALES with `conversion_location` PIXEL, or OUTCOME_TRAFFIC with WEBSITE. No other pairing is eligible.
  - Do not pass `product_set_id` — that builds an Advantage+ catalog carousel instead, and combining the two is rejected.
  - The ad account must have an eligible catalog product set, and must not be in a sensitive vertical.

  An explicit request that fails any of these is rejected with an actionable error — the creative is NOT silently created without Product Extensions. Check the conditions before offering it to the advertiser.

  **Placement-customized media ads:**
  - `ad_account_id`, `page_id`, `placement_customizations` (2–10 entries)
  - Each entry requires exactly one of `image_hash`, `image_url`, or `video_id`. Images and videos may be mixed in one creative.
  - Exactly one entry must be the fallback and omit every placement field. Every other entry requires `publisher_platforms` and may narrow delivery with the matching platform position fields. Rules may not overlap.
  - `link_url` is required when any entry is an image. Copy, link, display link, headline, description, and CTA are shared across all entries.
  - Do not provide top-level `video_id`, `image_hash`, `image_url`, `product_set_id`, `cards`, or `object_story_id`. `placement_videos` remains a supported video-only legacy alias; do not combine the two fields.
  - Image hashes are checked against this ad account. Image URLs are downloaded into the account and returned as hashes. Every video must exist, be visible to the caller, and have status `ready` before the creative write starts.

  **Multi-media ads (MMU):**
  - `ad_account_id`, `page_id`, `multi_media` (2–10 entries)
  - Each entry requires exactly one of `image_hash`, `image_url`, or `video_id`. Images and videos may be mixed.
  - Use MMU when Meta should choose the best asset at delivery time. There are no fallback or placement rules. For exact placement-to-asset mapping, use `placement_customizations` instead.
  - `link_url` is required when any entry is an image. Use `primary_texts`, `headlines`, and `descriptions` for up to five variants of each; Meta chooses the combination at delivery time. The singular `message`, `headline`, and `description` fields remain supported as one-variant aliases. Link, display link, and CTA are shared across the asset pool.
  - Do not combine `multi_media` with PAC, top-level media, `product_set_id`, `cards`, `object_story_id`, or a Partnership Ad.
  - Image URLs are downloaded into the ad account. Every image and video is checked before the creative write starts. The tool also supplies the MMU fields MAPI requires, including video thumbnails.

  **Advantage+ catalog carousel ads:**
  - `ad_account_id`, `page_id`, `product_set_id`, `link_url`
  - Do not provide `image_hash`, `image_url`, or `video_id` — catalog ads source media from the product catalog automatically.

  **Static carousel ads:**
  - `ad_account_id`, `page_id`, `cards` (2–10 cards)
  - Each card: one of `image_hash` or `image_url` (an image card), or `video_id` for a video card (a thumbnail is optional — if you omit `image_hash`/`image_url`, the video's default thumbnail is used). Per card you may also set `link`, `headline` (or `name`), `description`, and `call_to_action_type`.
  - Provide `cards` alone — do not combine with `image_hash`, `image_url`, `video_id`, or `product_set_id`. Top-level `link_url` and `call_to_action_type` act as per-card fallbacks; each image card must have a link (its own or the fallback), while video cards may omit the link. Under a click-to-messaging CTA the tool supplies card links instead, and a card with its own non-messaging `call_to_action_type` needs its own link or a top-level `link_url` (see below).

  **Boosted-post ads (boost an existing organic Facebook Page post):**
  - `ad_account_id`, `page_id`, `object_story_id` — the existing post as `{page_id}_{post_id}` (e.g. "1234567890_9876543210").
  - The `page_id` must match the page embedded in `object_story_id`. The post must still exist, be published, belong to that Page, and be visible/promotable by the caller. If it was deleted, unpublished, or is inaccessible, choose a current post or create an inline creative instead; retrying the same ID cannot repair it.
  - For an ad set optimized for link clicks, use an existing post only if that post already has a valid external destination and CTA. Existing-post copy and CTA cannot be added or repaired by this tool; use an inline creative with `link_url` and `call_to_action_type` when either is missing.
  - The post's existing media and copy are used as-is: do NOT also provide `image_hash`, `image_url`, `video_id`, `placement_customizations`, `placement_videos`, `multi_media`, `product_set_id`, `cards`, `link_url`, `message`, `primary_texts`, `description`, `descriptions`, `headline`, `headlines`, `call_to_action_type`, or `display_link`.
  - You may provide `instagram_user_id` for Instagram placement delivery.
  - This is a plain self-boost of the advertiser's own Page post (no partner). To boost a creator's post as branded content with a partner, use `facebook_partnership_ad` instead (below) — a top-level `object_story_id` is NOT a Partnership Ad.

  **Facebook Partnership Ads (branded content):**
  Boosts an existing Facebook branded-content post. A Partnership Ad always has two identities: `facebook_partnership_ad.sponsor_page_id` is always REQUIRED and names the partner Page, while the boosted post's own owner is the primary. Which Page you put in the sponsor slot is what makes the ad sponsor-led or creator-led — there is no separate mode field. Supplying the sponsor (or an ad code) under `facebook_partnership_ad` is what routes the request to a Partnership Ad rather than a plain boosted post. Creating a Facebook branded-content post inline from media is not supported.

  - Reference the source post with exactly one of `facebook_partnership_ad.facebook_boost_post_access_token` (the encrypted ad code a creator generated to authorize this advertiser) or `facebook_partnership_ad.object_story_id` (an existing branded-content post, formatted `<post_owner_page_id>_<post_id>`, the advertiser already has permission on).
  - Do not combine either with `image_hash`, `image_url`, `video_id`, `product_set_id`, or `cards` — the boost reuses the existing post's own media. Partnership Ads can run with an Advantage+ catalog, but only as a separate creative shape (a collection ad, a catalog-carousel intro card, or the "Show Products" optimization) — not by adding a `product_set_id` to this boost — and this tool does not build those catalog shapes yet.
  - `facebook_partnership_ad.ad_format` — optional header format, an integer; omit it unless the advertiser asked for a specific header. 1 = dual header (both identities — the default), 2 = single header, 3 = dynamic header (the identity shown is optimized at delivery).
  - To promote a creator's *Instagram* post that already exists, use `ads_boost_ig_post` — not this tool.

  **Instagram Partnership Ads (branded content, built from new media):**
  Builds a NEW branded-content creative rather than boosting a post the creator already published. Set `instagram_user_id` to the CREATOR's numeric account ID, username, `@handle`, or Instagram profile URL — their handle is what the ad runs under — and name the sponsoring brand in `instagram_partnership_ad.sponsor_instagram_user_id` and `.sponsor_page_id`. The tool resolves the creator to a professional account and derives its Page-compatible ads identity: either its linked Facebook Page or its Instagram Account Backed Page. Omit `page_id`, or provide that matching identity ID. Both sponsor fields are required together.

  - Unlike the Facebook object above, this one DOES take media: supply `image_hash`, `image_url`, `video_id` or `cards` as normal.
  - Cannot be combined with `object_story_id` or an ad code — those mean an existing post, which is `ads_boost_ig_post`'s job.
  - After creation, check `partnership_ad_verification_status`. `verified` means the server derived a real, currently usable Partnership Ad. `verification_pending` means it derived a real Partnership Ad whose asynchronous processing has not settled yet. `verified_with_issues` means processing settled with a real Partnership Ad that cannot deliver yet. `verified_not_ready` means it derived a real Partnership Ad, but the creative is not `ACTIVE` and is not in either expected processing state. For any value other than `verified`, relay `partnership_ad_message` and do not retry or attach the creative to an ad automatically.

  ## Click-to-messaging creatives (CTWA / CTM):
  Set `call_to_action_type` to a messaging CTA and the creative's button opens a chat thread instead of a web page. This is the creative half of a messaging ad; pair it with an ad set whose `destination_type` matches.

  | `call_to_action_type` | Opens | Ad set `destination_type` |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `WHATSAPP_MESSAGE` | WhatsApp (CTWA) | `WHATSAPP` |
  | `MESSAGE_PAGE` | Messenger (CTM) | `MESSENGER` |

  - **Omit `link_url`** for these. The click destination is the messaging thread, and the tool fills in the standard per-surface link. A `link_url` that already is that surface's link (e.g. `https://api.whatsapp.com/send?phone=…`) is replaced with the standard one; any other `link_url` is rejected.
  - The messaging destination is derived from `call_to_action_type` alone; there is no separate destination field to set.
  - The CTA must agree with the ad set's `destination_type` (table above) — a mismatch is rejected when the ad is created.
  - Click-to-messaging is rolling out per ad account, and where it is not enabled the creative gets no messaging button: the request fails (saying click-to-messaging is not enabled, or asking for `link_url`), or the creative is created without that button. A creative whose buttons open the messaging thread comes back with `click_to_messaging_destination` set to that surface (`WHATSAPP` or `MESSENGER`), which must match the ad set's `destination_type`. If the response lacks it, or the request failed that way, tell the advertiser click-to-messaging is not available for that ad account yet; do not retry with a `link_url`. `ads_get_creatives` cannot confirm this either way: it returns the same `call_to_action_type` and links whether or not the button opens the thread.
  - The WhatsApp business number is configured on the **Page**, not on the creative. This tool does not set a creative-level welcome message, so the Page's default greeting applies.
  - **WhatsApp prerequisite:** a WhatsApp ad can only run if the Page (or its Instagram account) has a verified WhatsApp Business number linked. Without one, the creative and a PAUSED ad are still created, but activating the ad fails with "Reconnect your WhatsApp number to your Facebook Page or Instagram account to run this ad." If you see that error, tell the advertiser to link and verify a WhatsApp number in the Page's WhatsApp settings, then retry the activation — do not recreate the creative.
  - Works with the image, single-video, and static-carousel formats. **Not** the catalog (DA) carousel: that format still requires `link_url`, because its link is the catalog destination.
  - For a static carousel, every messaging CTA in the creative, top-level and per-card, must open the same surface: the one the ad set's `destination_type` names. A card whose effective CTA is a messaging one gets its link from the tool the same way, so leave its `link` unset. A click-to-Messenger carousel must use `MESSAGE_PAGE` at the top level and on every card. On a click-to-WhatsApp carousel, a card with its own *non*-messaging CTA (e.g. `SHOP_NOW`) needs its own `link` unless the creative has a top-level `link_url`, even when there is no top-level CTA. It never inherits the messaging link, which would leave it pointing at a chat URL with no recipient. A non-messaging top-level `call_to_action_type` needs `link_url`, since the top-level button is the one every card without its own `call_to_action_type` uses.
  - End-to-end messaging ad: `ads_create_campaign` → `ads_create_ad_set` (`destination_type: WHATSAPP`) → `ads_create_creative` (`call_to_action_type: WHATSAPP_MESSAGE`) → `ads_create_ad`.

  ## Optional fields (all formats):
  - `message` — one body/primary-text value shown above the image, video, or carousel. For `multi_media`, use `primary_texts` instead when you want multiple variants. For carousel ads, may contain template strings like {{product.name}} filled from the catalog at delivery time.
  - `primary_texts` — `multi_media` only; 1–5 body/primary-text variants. Do not combine with `message`. Meta chooses among them at delivery time.
  - `display_link` — the short URL/domain shown on the ad (for example `Verizon.com`). This is presentation text, not the click destination; continue to put the destination in `link_url` (a click-to-messaging creative takes none). Must be URL-shaped (a bare domain is fine); arbitrary text is rejected. Maps to Marketing API `caption`, including the CTA caption used by video creatives. The link line that shows it is being removed from Facebook mobile Feed for single-image and single-video ads, so it may not be visible there.
  - `description` — one short description value under the headline. For `multi_media`, use `descriptions` instead when you want multiple variants. Facebook Feed does not display it on single-image or single-video ads and Instagram has no description line, so tell the user it may not be visible. For carousels, prefer per-card `cards[].description`. On a single-video ad this maps to `video_data.link_description`, which the backend rejects without a call to action; this tool attaches the CTA only when `link_url` is present or `call_to_action_type` is a click-to-messaging CTA, so also provide `link_url` when you set `description` on a video ad, unless its `call_to_action_type` is a click-to-messaging one.
  - `descriptions` — `multi_media` only; 1–5 short-description variants. Do not combine with `description`. Meta chooses among them at delivery time.
  - `headline` — one short headline shown under the image, video, or carousel cards. For `multi_media`, use `headlines` instead when you want multiple variants.
  - `headlines` — `multi_media` only; 1–5 headline variants. Do not combine with `headline`. Meta chooses among them at delivery time.
  - `call_to_action_type` — CTA button type (defaults to LEARN_MORE). Must be an exact UPPER_CASE value from the accepted enum — arbitrary values are rejected. The messaging values WHATSAPP_MESSAGE / MESSAGE_PAGE make this a click-to-messaging creative — see that section above. See the field description for the full accepted list. Telephone CTAs (CALL, CALL_NOW, CALL_ME, MISSED_CALL) are not supported because they require a tel: destination, which this tool cannot supply. Use a supported CTA such as CONTACT_US, or create the telephone CTA in Ads Manager.
  - `name` — name of this ad creative as seen in the ad account's library. Strongly recommended.
  - `instagram_user_id` — IG user (Instagram Business Account) ID for IG placement delivery. For `instagram_partnership_ad`, this instead accepts the creator's numeric account ID, username, `@handle`, or Instagram profile URL. Omit it from other formats and the creative will not deliver on Instagram surfaces.
  - `self_ai_disclosure` — AI-generated content disclosure. "OPT_IN" declares the creative contains third-party AI-generated/edited media; "OPT_OUT" declares it does not. Omit if unknown. When opted in, Meta may display an "AI info" label on the ad; whether it appears depends on the ad's delivery regions and their AI-transparency requirements. Decide this before you create the creative — no update tool can set it afterwards. Always list this field for the advertiser so they can decide; disclosure is their responsibility, so never set or infer a value on their behalf. The declaration takes effect only where AI-transparency rules require it — currently the European Region, India, Taiwan, California, and New York.
  - `advantage_plus_creative` — set true to turn on the master Advantage+ Creative feature. Set false to leave that master feature off; false does not override a supplied `degrees_of_freedom_spec`.
  - `advantage_plus_creative_features` — specific Advantage+ Creative feature names (exact lower_snake_case, e.g. "image_touchups", "text_optimizations") to opt into individually. Use only when the advertiser asks for specific enhancements; most callers only need `advantage_plus_creative`.
  - `degrees_of_freedom_spec` — the raw Marketing API degrees_of_freedom_spec, for feature opt-outs or per-feature customizations. Do not combine it with `advantage_plus_creative=true` or a non-empty `advantage_plus_creative_features` list. It may be combined with `advantage_plus_creative=false` while preserving the raw spec.

  ## When to use:
  - The user wants a click-to-WhatsApp or click-to-Messenger ad creative (set the matching messaging `call_to_action_type`).
  - The user wants to create a single-image link ad creative from a pre-uploaded image.
  - The user wants to create a single-video ad creative from a pre-uploaded video.
  - The user wants to use different images, videos, or both for different placements, with one fallback asset.
  - The user wants Meta to optimize delivery across a pool of images, videos, or both, without fixed placement rules.
  - The user wants to create an Advantage+ catalog carousel ad creative from a product set.
  - The user wants to create a static carousel ad creative from a list of manually specified cards.
  - The user wants to boost an existing organic Page post (create a creative from an existing post via top-level `object_story_id`).
  - The user wants to create a Facebook Partnership Ad from an existing branded-content post.
  - The user wants to create an Instagram Partnership Ad from new image, video, or carousel media.

  ## Safe flexible-media workflow:
  1. If the user supplies multiple assets without explicitly choosing a format, do not guess or call this tool. Ask: "Do you want a carousel with swipeable cards, specific assets assigned to placements, or Meta to optimize across an asset pool?"
  2. Choose one mode: `placement_customizations` for exact placement rules, or `multi_media` for a delivery-optimized asset pool.
  3. Check the matching `applied_placement_customizations` or `applied_multi_media` response.
  4. Call `ads_create_ad` with `creative` set to `{"creative_id":"<CREATIVE_ID>"}`. That tool creates the ad in PAUSED state.
  5. Call `ads_get_ad_preview` for the intended Feed, Stories, and Reels placements. Keep the ad paused until a person approves it.

  ## When NOT to use:
  - Lead-gen or app-install creatives — not supported.
  - The user wants the creative attached to an ad in the same call — this tool only creates the creative.

  ## Catalog carousel — verify before you create:
  - Discover a valid `product_set_id` with `ads_catalog_list_product_sets` (list sets for a catalog) or `ads_catalog_list_products` (preview which products match a filter).
  - Check catalog health with `ads_catalog_get_diagnostics` (policy/data issues that block delivery) and `ads_catalog_get_dynamic_ads_health` (DA-specific checks) before relying on a catalog carousel to deliver. A non-empty but unhealthy catalog/product set can cause the new creative's ads to never deliver.

  ## Response:
  Returns the new `creative_id` plus echoed `name` and `account_id`. PAC returns `applied_placement_customizations`; MMU returns `applied_multi_media`. These show the normalized assets submitted to MAPI. A creative whose buttons open a messaging thread returns `click_to_messaging_destination`. For an Instagram Partnership Ad, attach the creative to an ad only when `partnership_ad_verification_status` is `verified`. Use `ads_get_creatives` afterward to inspect the created creative.
  When `warnings` is present, the creative WAS created, but some inputs were stored without being displayed on common placements. Relay every warning to the user; do not report a clean success without them.

  ## Known limitations:
  - Top-level image and video-thumbnail hashes are not prevalidated. Image hashes inside `placement_customizations` and `multi_media` are checked against the ad account before the creative write.
  - Duplicate detection: if a creative with identical content already exists and is active on the account, the existing `creative_id` is returned instead of creating a new one — your "new" creative may be a reused old one.
  - Creative content, including `display_link`, is immutable after publication. To change it, create a replacement creative and attach that replacement to the ad.
  - No support for `instagram_actor_id`, `effective_authorization_category` (political/issue ads), `url_tags`, or `applink_treatment`.
  - Placement customization changes the image or video asset. Text, link, display link, headline, description, and CTA are shared across placements.
  - MMU supports up to five ad-level primary-text, headline, and description variants. Per-media text, destination, crop, placement-exclusion, and audience-persona fields are not exposed yet.
  - Boosting covers Facebook Page posts only. Boosting an existing Instagram post is not supported, and `object_story_id` accepts only the plain `{page_id}_{post_id}` form — not substory or timeline-aggregate post tokens.

ad_account_id.description: Parent ad account ID, numeric (e.g. "123456789").

page_id.description: Facebook Page ID that will own the creative post. Required for every format except instagram_partnership_ad. For an Instagram Partnership Ad, omit this field and the tool derives the creator's Page-compatible ads identity (its linked Facebook Page or Instagram Account Backed Page); if provided, it must match that identity. For a Facebook Partnership Ad, set it to the Page publishing the ad. Must be a Page ID: if the owner is a Professional-mode or Profile-Plus creator, use their delegate Page ID, not their profile ID.

image_hash.description: Hash of a pre-uploaded image asset. For image ads: the ad image (required — exactly one of image_hash or image_url). For single-video ads: the video thumbnail / cover image shown before the video plays (required — exactly one of image_hash or image_url). For PAC or MMU, put image_hash inside placement_customizations or multi_media instead. Not used for catalog carousel ads.

image_url.description: URL of an image. For image ads: the ad image (required — exactly one of image_hash or image_url). For single-video ads: the video thumbnail / cover image shown before the video plays (required — exactly one of image_hash or image_url). For PAC or MMU, put image_url inside placement_customizations or multi_media instead. Not used for catalog carousel ads.

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video on the ad account. Required for a single-video ad, but not sufficient by itself: also provide exactly one of image_hash or image_url as the video thumbnail / cover image. For PAC or MMU, put video_id inside placement_customizations or multi_media instead. Not used for catalog carousel ads.

product_set_id.description: ID of a product set from the advertiser's catalog. Required for Advantage+ catalog carousel ads. When provided, creates a carousel creative that dynamically populates card content from the catalog at delivery time. Do not provide image_hash, image_url, or video_id when using product_set_id.

objective.description: Objective of the campaign this creative is for. REQUIRED when you request Product Extensions (together with conversion_location and link_url) — an explicit Product Extensions request that omits it is rejected. Only these two objectives are eligible for Product Extensions; a campaign on any other objective cannot use it. Omit this field when you are not requesting Product Extensions.

conversion_location.description: Conversion location of the campaign this creative is for. REQUIRED when you request Product Extensions (together with objective and link_url) — an explicit Product Extensions request that omits it is rejected. Pair PIXEL with objective OUTCOME_SALES, or WEBSITE with OUTCOME_TRAFFIC; no other pairing is eligible. Omit this field when you are not requesting Product Extensions.

link_url.description: Destination URL the creative clicks to (e.g. "https://example.com/landing"). Required for image ads, catalog carousel ads, and PAC or MMU containing an image; optional for single-video, video-only PAC, and video-only MMU. Always include https:// scheme; if omitted the tool prepends it automatically. For catalog carousel ads, this is the default landing URL; product-specific deep links from the catalog may override it at delivery time. Do NOT set this for a click-to-messaging image, video, or static-carousel creative (call_to_action_type WHATSAPP_MESSAGE / MESSAGE_PAGE): the click opens a chat thread and the tool supplies the standard link for that messaging surface. A link that already is that surface's link (e.g. https://api.whatsapp.com/send) is replaced with the standard one; any other link is rejected. Catalog carousel ads are the exception — they always require link_url, since it names the catalog destination, and a messaging CTA does not waive it.

display_link.description: Short URL or domain displayed on the ad (e.g. "Verizon.com"). This is presentation text, not the destination URL; put the click destination in link_url (a click-to-messaging creative takes none). Must be URL-shaped — a bare domain is fine, arbitrary text like "Shop now" is rejected. Supported for image, single-video, PAC, MMU, static-carousel, and Advantage+ catalog-carousel creatives. link_url is required when display_link is provided, except for a click-to-messaging creative. Immutable after the creative is published. The link line that shows it is being removed from Facebook mobile Feed for single-image and single-video ads, so it may not be visible there; the response carries a warning when that applies.

message.description: One body/primary-text value shown above the image, video, or carousel. Shared across all placement_customizations entries. For multi_media, use primary_texts instead when you want multiple variants. For carousel ads, may contain template strings like {{product.name}} filled from the catalog at delivery time.

primary_texts.description: For multi_media only: 1–5 body/primary-text variants. Meta chooses among them at delivery time. Do not combine with message; put every variant in this array. For other creative formats, use message.

description.description: One short description value. Shared across all placement_customizations entries. For multi_media, use descriptions instead when you want multiple variants. Maps to link_data.description for image ads, video_data.link_description for video ads, or template_data.description for carousel ads. Facebook Feed does not display it on single-image or single-video ads and Instagram has no description line; the response carries a warning when that applies. For single-video ads, video_data.link_description is rejected without a call to action, and this tool attaches one only when link_url is set or call_to_action_type is a click-to-messaging CTA (WHATSAPP_MESSAGE / MESSAGE_PAGE) — so also provide link_url when you use description on a video ad, unless call_to_action_type is a click-to-messaging one (any other call_to_action_type alone, without link_url, is ignored).

descriptions.description: For multi_media only: 1–5 short-description variants. Meta chooses among them at delivery time. Do not combine with description; put every variant in this array. For other creative formats, use description.

call_to_action_type.description: Call-to-action button type. Defaults to LEARN_MORE if omitted. Must be an exact UPPER_CASE value from the backend CTA enum — do NOT invent or reformat a value, or the request is rejected with "call_to_action[type] must be one of the following values: …". Use one of the accepted values below; pick the one whose label matches the user's intent — do NOT guess. CTA destination is auto-set to link_url, except for the click-to-messaging values below, which instead open a chat thread on their messaging surface and need no link_url (a link to that same surface is replaced with the standard one, and any other link is rejected): WHATSAPP_MESSAGE opens WhatsApp (pair with an ad set destination_type of WHATSAPP), MESSAGE_PAGE opens Messenger (MESSENGER). Telephone CTAs (CALL, CALL_NOW, CALL_ME, MISSED_CALL) are not supported because they require a tel: destination, which this tool cannot supply. Use a supported CTA such as CONTACT_US, or create the telephone CTA in Ads Manager. Accepted values by category: — Shopping: SHOP_NOW (Shop Now), BUY_NOW (Buy Now), ORDER_NOW (Order Now), START_ORDER (Start Order), ADD_TO_CART (Add to Cart), SEE_SHOP (See Shop), BROWSE_SHOP (Browse Shop), VIEW_PRODUCT (View Product), BUY (Buy), SELL_NOW (Sell Now), SHOP_WITH_AI (Shop with AI). — General: LEARN_MORE (Learn More), SIGN_UP (Sign Up), OPEN_LINK (Open Link), GET_STARTED (Get Started), SEE_MORE (See More), FIND_OUT_MORE (Find Out More), VISIT_WEBSITE (Visit Website), GET_DETAILS (Get Details), CONFIRM (Confirm), NO_BUTTON (No Button). — Contact: CONTACT_US (Contact Us), CONTACT (Contact), GET_QUOTE (Get Quote), GET_A_QUOTE (Get a Quote), MESSAGE_PAGE (Message Page), WHATSAPP_MESSAGE (WhatsApp Message), GET_IN_TOUCH (Get in Touch), AUDIO_CALL (Audio Call), VIDEO_CALL (Video Call), EMAIL_NOW (Email Now), ASK_A_QUESTION (Ask a Question), CHAT_NOW (Chat Now), CHAT_WITH_US (Chat with Us), ASK_FOR_MORE_INFO (Ask for More Info). — Booking: BOOK_NOW (Book Now), BOOK_TRAVEL (Book Travel), REQUEST_TIME (Request Time), MAKE_AN_APPOINTMENT (Make an Appointment), BOOK_A_CONSULTATION (Book a Consultation), GET_SHOWTIMES (Get Showtimes), BUY_TICKETS (Buy Tickets). — App: INSTALL_APP (Install App), INSTALL_MOBILE_APP (Install Mobile App), USE_APP (Use App), USE_MOBILE_APP (Use Mobile App), DOWNLOAD (Download), PLAY_GAME (Play Game), OPEN_INSTANT_APP (Open Instant App), UPDATE_APP (Update App). — Lead Gen: APPLY_NOW (Apply Now), INQUIRE_NOW (Inquire Now), GET_OFFER (Get Offer), GET_DIRECTIONS (Get Directions). — Engagement: SUBSCRIBE (Subscribe), FOLLOW_PAGE (Follow Page), EVENT_RSVP (RSVP), DONATE (Donate), DONATE_NOW (Donate Now), RAISE_MONEY (Raise Money), REFER_FRIENDS (Refer Friends). — Media: WATCH_VIDEO (Watch Video), WATCH_MORE (Watch More), LISTEN_NOW (Listen Now), LISTEN_MUSIC (Listen Music), WATCH_LIVE_VIDEO (Watch Live Video).

name.description: Name of this ad creative as seen in the ad account's library. Strongly recommended.

headline.description: One short headline shown under the image (link_data.name), video (video_data.title), or carousel cards (template_data.name). Shared across all placement_customizations entries. For multi_media, use headlines instead when you want multiple variants.

headlines.description: For multi_media only: 1–5 headline variants. Meta chooses among them at delivery time. Do not combine with headline; put every variant in this array. For other creative formats, use headline.

instagram_user_id.description: Instagram User (IG Business Account) ID for IG placement delivery. For instagram_partnership_ad this is required and identifies the creator; it accepts a numeric account ID, username, @handle, or Instagram profile URL, resolves it to a professional account, and derives page_id from the creator's linked Facebook Page or Instagram Account Backed Page. For other formats, only a numeric account ID is accepted; omit it to exclude Instagram placements.

self_ai_disclosure.description: AI-generated content disclosure for the creative. Set to "OPT_IN" to declare that this creative contains media created or edited with a third-party generative AI tool; set to "OPT_OUT" to declare it does not. Omit if unknown. Only these two exact UPPER_CASE values are accepted. When you opt in, Meta may display an "AI info" label on the ad; whether it appears depends on the regions the ad is delivered to and their AI-transparency requirements. Decide this before creating the creative — no update tool can set it afterwards. Always list this field for the advertiser so they can decide; disclosure is their responsibility, so never set or infer a value on their behalf. The declaration takes effect only where AI-transparency rules require it — currently the European Region, India, Taiwan, California, and New York.

object_story_id.description: ID of an existing organic Page post to boost, as {page_id}_{post_id} (e.g. "1234567890_9876543210"). The embedded page must match page_id. Both halves must be canonical IDs: {page_id} is a Page ID (for a Professional-mode or Profile-Plus creator, their delegate Page ID — not their profile ID), and {post_id} is the post's own ID — not the ID of a photo, video, or other attachment on it. The post must still exist, be published, belong to that Page, and be visible/promotable by the caller; retrying a deleted, unpublished, or inaccessible post cannot repair it. For an ad set optimized for link clicks, the post must already contain a valid external destination and CTA because existing-post copy and CTA cannot be added here. The post media and copy are used as-is, so do NOT combine this with image_hash, image_url, video_id, placement_customizations, placement_videos, product_set_id, cards, link_url, message, primary_texts, description, descriptions, headline, headlines, call_to_action_type, or display_link. instagram_user_id may be provided for Instagram placement delivery.

advantage_plus_creative.description: Turn on Advantage+ Creative — Meta's automatic per-impression creative optimizations (image brightness/contrast, text improvements, and similar). This is the master toggle most callers want. Set true to enable it. Set false to leave the master feature off; false does not override a supplied degrees_of_freedom_spec. Only set true when the advertiser wants Meta to automatically optimize the creative.

advantage_plus_creative_features.description: Specific Advantage+ Creative feature names to opt the creative into individually. Each entry must be an exact lower_snake_case feature name (e.g. "image_touchups", "text_optimizations", "image_animation"). Most callers only need advantage_plus_creative; use this only when the advertiser asks for specific enhancements.

degrees_of_freedom_spec.description: Raw Marketing API degrees_of_freedom_spec, passed as a JSON-ENCODED STRING (NOT a nested JSON object) — e.g. "{\"creative_features_spec\":{\"text_optimizations\":{\"enroll_status\":\"OPT_OUT\"}}}". Use only for what the advantage_plus_creative / advantage_plus_creative_features shortcuts cannot express: opting a feature OUT, or per-feature customizations. Do not combine it with advantage_plus_creative=true or a non-empty advantage_plus_creative_features list. It may be combined with advantage_plus_creative=false while preserving the raw spec.

cards.description: Cards for a STATIC carousel ad (2–10). Distinct from Advantage+ catalog carousel: do NOT combine cards with product_set_id, image_hash, image_url, video_id, placement_customizations, placement_videos, or multi_media. Each card needs exactly one image (image_hash or image_url); a video card sets video_id and may omit the image, in which case the video's default thumbnail is used. Top-level link_url and call_to_action_type act as per-card fallbacks.

items.description: A single static carousel card.

image_hash.description: Hash of a pre-uploaded image for this card. Provide exactly one of image_hash or image_url. Required for an image card; optional for a video card (used as the thumbnail, otherwise the video's default thumbnail is used).

image_url.description: URL of the image for this card. Provide exactly one of image_hash or image_url. Required for an image card; optional for a video card (used as the thumbnail, otherwise the video's default thumbnail is used).

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video for this card (makes it a video card). A thumbnail is optional: if you omit image_hash/image_url, the video's default thumbnail is used automatically.

link.description: Destination URL for this card. Falls back to the top-level link_url when omitted; https:// is prepended if missing. Required for image cards (via card link or the top-level fallback); optional for video cards. Omit it for a card whose effective call_to_action_type (its own, else the top-level one) is a click-to-messaging CTA: the tool supplies that surface's link, replacing a link to the same surface and rejecting any other. On a click-to-WhatsApp carousel, a card with its own non-messaging call_to_action_type needs this link unless there is a top-level link_url, even when there is no top-level call_to_action_type — it never inherits the messaging link. A click-to-Messenger carousel cannot include a non-messaging card.

headline.description: Short headline shown on this card (child_attachments.name). Alias: name.

name.description: Alias for headline (matches ads_get_creatives output). Used only when headline is not set.

description.description: Description text shown on this card (child_attachments.description).

call_to_action_type.description: Per-card CTA button type (same accepted values as the top-level call_to_action_type). Falls back to the top-level call_to_action_type. A messaging CTA here must open the same surface as every other messaging CTA in the creative, the one the ad set's destination_type names. On a click-to-WhatsApp carousel, a non-messaging value here requires this card to set its own link unless there is a top-level link_url; a click-to-Messenger carousel must use MESSAGE_PAGE on every card.

placement_customizations.description: Placement Asset Customization (2–10 assets). Each entry contains exactly one of image_hash, image_url, or video_id. Exactly one entry is the fallback and contains no placement fields. Other entries need non-empty publisher_platforms; placement rules and media assets may not repeat or overlap. When one asset serves multiple platforms, combine those platforms and their positions in one entry instead of repeating the asset in separate entries. Never reuse an override asset as the fallback. If the request has no fallback, ask for one and do not call the tool. Do not combine with multi_media, placement_videos, or top-level media fields.

items.description: One image or video and the non-overlapping placements where it should be used.

image_hash.description: Hash of a pre-uploaded image in this ad account. Provide exactly one of image_hash, image_url, or video_id.

image_url.description: Absolute http/https image URL. The tool downloads it into this ad account and uses the resulting image hash. Provide exactly one media field.

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video. It must be accessible and fully processed (ready). Provide exactly one media field.

publisher_platforms.description: Platforms for this asset: facebook, instagram, messenger, audience_network, threads, whatsapp, or oculus. Omit this and all position fields on exactly one entry to make it the fallback asset.

facebook_positions.description: Optional Facebook positions, such as feed, story, facebook_reels, marketplace, instream_video, or right_hand_column. Requires facebook in publisher_platforms.

instagram_positions.description: Optional Instagram positions: stream, story, reels, explore, explore_home, profile_feed, profile_reels, ig_search, reels_overlay, or shop. Requires instagram in publisher_platforms.

messenger_positions.description: Optional Messenger positions: sponsored_messages, messenger_home, story, or marketing_messages. Requires messenger in publisher_platforms.

audience_network_positions.description: Optional Audience Network positions: classic, instream_video, rewarded_video, or ctv_instream_video. Requires audience_network in publisher_platforms.

threads_positions.description: Optional Threads positions: threads_stream. Requires threads in publisher_platforms.

whatsapp_positions.description: Optional WhatsApp positions: status, marketing_messages, channel, or smb_marketing_messages. Requires whatsapp in publisher_platforms.

multi_media.description: Multi-media optimization (MMU) asset pool with 2–10 unique images, videos, or both. Meta chooses which eligible asset to deliver. Pair it with primary_texts, headlines, and descriptions for up to five variants of each; use the singular message, headline, and description fields only when you want one value. This field does not set exact placement rules or a fallback; use placement_customizations for that. Do not combine with placement_customizations, placement_videos, top-level media, product_set_id, cards, object_story_id, or facebook_partnership_ad.

items.description: One image or video in the delivery-optimized MMU asset pool.

image_hash.description: Hash of a pre-uploaded image in this ad account. Provide exactly one of image_hash, image_url, or video_id.

image_url.description: Absolute http/https image URL. The tool downloads it into this ad account and uses the resulting image hash. Provide exactly one media field.

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video. It must be accessible and fully processed. The tool uses its default thumbnail. Provide exactly one media field.

placement_videos.description: Legacy video-only Placement Asset Customization input (2–10). New calls should use placement_customizations. Exactly one entry must be a fallback that contains only video_id. Other entries require non-empty publisher_platforms. Rules and videos may not repeat or overlap. Do not combine with placement_customizations, multi_media, or top-level media fields.

items.description: A pre-uploaded video and the placements where it should be used.

video_id.description: ID of a pre-uploaded video on the ad account.

publisher_platforms.description: Platforms for this video: facebook, instagram, messenger, audience_network, threads, whatsapp, or oculus. Omit this and all position fields on exactly one entry to make it the fallback video.

facebook_positions.description: Optional Facebook positions, such as feed, story, facebook_reels, marketplace, instream_video, or right_hand_column. Requires facebook in publisher_platforms.

instagram_positions.description: Optional Instagram positions: stream, story, reels, explore, explore_home, profile_feed, profile_reels, ig_search, reels_overlay, or shop. Requires instagram in publisher_platforms.

messenger_positions.description: Optional Messenger positions: sponsored_messages, messenger_home, story, or marketing_messages. Requires messenger in publisher_platforms.

audience_network_positions.description: Optional Audience Network positions: classic, instream_video, rewarded_video, or ctv_instream_video. Requires audience_network in publisher_platforms.

threads_positions.description: Optional Threads positions: threads_stream. Requires threads in publisher_platforms.

whatsapp_positions.description: Optional WhatsApp positions: status, marketing_messages, channel, or smb_marketing_messages. Requires whatsapp in publisher_platforms.

facebook_partnership_ad.description: Facebook Partnership Ad (branded content) created from an existing post — via an ad code (facebook_boost_post_access_token) or by referencing the post directly (object_story_id). Provide this object to create a Partnership Ad — do NOT also provide image_hash, image_url, video_id, multi_media, product_set_id, or cards. To build a new Instagram Partnership Ad creative from media instead, use instagram_partnership_ad; to boost a creator's existing Instagram post, use ads_boost_ig_post.

facebook_boost_post_access_token.description: Encrypted ad code (a.k.a. "boost post access token") that a Facebook creator generated to authorize this advertiser to boost one of the creator's existing Facebook posts as a Facebook Partnership Ad. Provide exactly one of facebook_boost_post_access_token or object_story_id.

object_story_id.description: Reference to an existing Facebook branded-content post to boost, formatted "<post_owner_page_id>_<post_id>". The page half is the Page ID of the post's owner (for a Professional-mode or Profile-Plus owner, their delegate Page ID, not their profile ID); the post half must be the post's own ID, not the ID of an attachment on it. Use when the advertiser already has permission on the post (instead of an ad code). Provide exactly one of facebook_boost_post_access_token or object_story_id.

ad_format.description: Partnership Ad header format, as an integer. Optional; omit it unless the advertiser asked for a specific header, in which case: 1 = dual header (both identities, the default), 2 = single header, 3 = dynamic (optimized at delivery).

sponsor_page_id.description: REQUIRED. Facebook Page ID of the Partnership Ad's secondary identity (the boosted post's owner is the primary). In a sponsor boost it is the Page publishing the ad, the same value as page_id; in a creator boost it is the partner Page. Must be a Page ID — for a Professional-mode or Profile-Plus partner, their delegate Page ID, not their profile ID.

instagram_partnership_ad.description: Instagram Partnership Ad (branded content) built from new media in this same call. Unlike facebook_partnership_ad, this one DOES carry media — supply image_hash, image_url, video_id or cards as usual. Set instagram_user_id to the CREATOR's numeric account ID, username, @handle, or Instagram profile URL; page_id is derived from the resolved creator's linked Facebook Page or Instagram Account Backed Page unless that matching identity ID is provided. The two fields here name the sponsoring brand. To promote a post the creator has already published, use ads_boost_ig_post instead — this object is for a new creative only, and cannot be combined with object_story_id.

sponsor_instagram_user_id.description: REQUIRED. Instagram account ID of the sponsoring brand. This is what distinguishes an Instagram Partnership Ad from a Facebook one, so it must be the brand and never the creator — the creator goes in the top-level instagram_user_id.

sponsor_page_id.description: REQUIRED. Facebook Page ID of the same sponsoring brand. Both sponsor fields are required together: supplying only one leaves the brand half-identified and the ad would be created as an ordinary one.

advertiser_request.description: Capture what the advertiser is actually asking for, in their exact words, quoted from their own messages word for word wherever you can. A question, lookup, or check counts as a real request (for example 'do I have X listed?', 'show me my Y', 'how many Z are left?'), so capture it. Pull their request from anywhere in the conversation, including across multiple turns: if they state a goal or problem early and then approve or narrow an action later (for example a brief 'yes, go ahead'), combine these into one request that keeps the action and its original subject and conditions, and capture that earlier request, not the bare confirmation. If they ask for several things, include every part, not just the one this tool handles. Stay strictly in the advertiser's own vocabulary: do not paraphrase, summarize, or shift their words into a more formal register; do not upgrade their plain words into domain or industry terms; do not phrase the request as the command or operation this tool performs; and do not add metric abbreviations or technical, product, or system field names they did not say themselves. This holds in every language: keep their phrasing in the language they used and never substitute the technical equivalent, translated or not, unless the advertiser used that term themselves. Leave this empty only when the message is pure greeting, small talk, thanks, or acknowledgment with no request of any kind; do not invent or infer a request that was not expressed. Do not include names, contact details, or other personal information.

advertiser_job.description: Classify the user's primary current job using the advertiser-job taxonomy. Keep the same value across all tool calls for this request.

client_conversation_id.description: Required on every call. Send this field with every Meta Ads tool call you make. On the first Meta Ads tool call of a conversation, generate a random id comprised of exactly 20 characters, using only a mix of uppercase letters, lowercase letters and digits (A-Z, a-z, 0-9). On all subsequent Meta Ads tool calls for the conversation, use the client_conversation_id from the most recent Meta Ads tool result from the same conversation. If none returned one, reuse the last valid ID you sent. Never send this value to a tool from a different MCP server or product. Generate a new id only when a genuinely new conversation begins. Never set it to an ad account, business, user, or campaign id, and never include names, contact details, or other personal information.

tools.name: ads_create_custom_audience
tools.description:
Creates a custom audience under an ad account. Supported subtypes are CUSTOM
(customer list), WEBSITE, ENGAGEMENT, MOBILE_APP, and LOOKALIKE.

## When to use

Use this tool only to create a new custom audience.

- Use ads_update_custom_audience_users to add or remove customer-list users.
- Use ads_update_custom_audience to modify an existing audience.
- Use ads_delete_custom_audience to delete an audience.

## Subtype requirements

### CUSTOM

- Requires customer_file_source.
- Creates an empty audience. After creation, use
  ads_update_custom_audience_users to upload users.
- Set is_value_based=true only when uploaded rows will include customer values.
- retention_days must be between 1 and 180.

### WEBSITE

- Requires rule with a "pixel" event source and pixel ID. If the pixel ID is
  unknown, use ads_get_datasets.
- The audience populates automatically from pixel events.
- Supported templates include ALL_VISITORS for all website visitors,
  VISITORS_BY_URL for URL or event filters, and TOP_TIME_SPENDERS for
  percentile-based time-spent audiences.
